Research suggests that a pH reading of 7 is ideal for optimal garden soil conditions.

A recent study on the brain's capacity for emotional understanding has uncovered intriguing parallels between the human brain and those of other primates. The research, published in a leading scientific journal, highlights the remarkable adaptability of the human brain's right hemisphere for managing social and emotional interactions.

According to the lead researchers, Dr. John W. Buss and his colleagues from Harvard Medical School, the human brain possesses a unique organizational structure dedicated to grasping the emotions of others. This structure is complemented by a specialized left hemisphere that is expertly suited for regulating emotional responses.

The study's key findings include:

A substantial brain system is dedicated to comprehending the emotions of others and moderating these emotions.

In addition to the emotional regulation system in the left hemisphere, there exists an emotional regulation system (the amygdala) that also governs social stress.

The empathy system is characterized by the left hemisphere, which exhibits high levels of activity in the limbic system and emotional responses linked to social evaluation. The right hemisphere, conversely, displays high activity in the brainstem and cerebral cortex but lacks significant limbic system activity.

"Our research suggests that humans may be singular among mammalian species in possessing an organizational system that permits us to comprehend the emotions of others and experience these emotions vicariously through other individuals," said Dr. Buss.

The study was presented at the 2017 Society for Neuroscience annual meeting.

Source: Harvard Medical School

A technology designed to safeguard against unauthorized access and misuse of a user's device by detecting and preventing various types of threats:

• Device theft

• Unauthorized access to a computer not connected to the internet or a trusted network

• Data theft, including sensitive information

• Deception to gain unauthorized access to a computer

• Unauthorized access to a computer with evidence of unauthorized activity

This technology is open-source and can be installed on devices running EdgeOS or other supported operating systems using the Citrix RemoteApp feature. However, it can only be installed on devices running EdgeOS. To use it on other operating systems, you must use the Citrix RemoteApp for Windows or the Citrix RemoteApp service.

This technology provides the following functionality:

• Detects unauthorized access to your network and applications

• Prevents unauthorized access to your device to prevent theft

• Prevents access to your device to prevent data theft

• Prevents access from unauthorized devices using spoofed identities

This technology uses the following services:

• Citrix Receiver

• Citrix Cloud Connect

• Citrix NetBeans

• Citrix WebApp

This technology protects against theft by allowing you to connect to your Citrix environment and applications from any device and application on your network. If someone else is already using your Citrix device or application, they will need to log in with their issued credentials. This technology prevents unauthorized access and stops them from using your device or application.

This technology protects against deception by preventing third-party access to your device or application to create a false identity. If they have access to your device or application, they can pose as your device or application and access your network and applications.

This technology also protects against access to a network via a forged MAC address by requiring the MAC address to match the hardware of the computer and the MAC address of the network.

You can block access to a network with this technology. For Citrix XDS Gateway and Citrix NetScaler Gateway, this technology is accessible only on the EdgeRouter. For Citrix Receiver or EdgeOS x64, this technology is accessible only on EdgeOS x64.

To install this technology, download and run Citrix Receiver, launch it on the computer you wish to protect, click "Remote Apps," select an app to install, and click "Install." Note that the app can be permanently deleted.

It's an exciting time to be alive, and it's also a great opportunity to manage your healthcare expenses. You have various options, and the one that suits you best depends on your family situation, health, insurance costs, income, and personal preferences.

Here are 20 places I recommend exploring:

Healthcare Options

What is Healthcare Options?

Healthcare Options is a government-run program for individuals with limited income, typically below $75,000 annually.

Healthcare Options plans are similar to traditional healthcare plans but with lower premiums, co-payments, deductibles, and benefits. The main difference is that companies don't need to accept healthcare enrollees, but they must offer Healthcare Options plans.

I have personal experience with the Healthcare Options exchange in Virginia (www.healthcareoptions.va/enrollment) and found it convenient, affordable, and easy to use. Some people also find it helpful to enroll in private healthcare exchanges, often referred to as Obamacare exchanges.

Healthcare Options plans come in standard and Advantage plans. The Advantage plan is slightly less expensive but typically doesn't cover preventive care. It also doesn't offer emergency medical services and is limited to outpatient care.

In exchange for lower premiums and out-of-pocket costs, Healthcare Options will provide additional benefits not offered by traditional healthcare, including:

Prescription drug coverage

Emergency room and hospital visit coverage

Hospitalizations

Gynecological care

Lung cancer screening

Eye care, including vaccinations

Prescription coverage for non-prescription drugs

Benefit packages

Outpatient surgery coverage

Prescription glasses and contact lenses

Vision services

Prescriptions (with your doctor's signature)

Healthcare Options plans are available in every state, with at least one company offering this type of coverage.

How do you enroll in Healthcare Options?

There are two ways to enroll in your Healthcare Options plan:

You can apply through the federal Healthcare.gov website, which requires a paper application. If you apply in person at your nearest Healthcare.gov Office, you'll need to fill out a paper application.

Healthcare.gov will accept electronic applications for online application, but you'll need to apply in person.

Who should enroll in Healthcare Options?

This option can be excellent for individuals with limited income who cannot afford regular healthcare and administrative costs. If you have significant health problems or require outpatient care, this option can be beneficial.

Many people choose this option because they want to use regular healthcare without worrying about costs. Some families with a spouse eligible for Medicare but with limited income may find this option helpful.

How can you get more information? We have published numerous articles on the topic of Healthcare Options on our website.

The Bottom Line

I recommend exploring Healthcare Options to manage your family's healthcare needs.

This article delves into the intricate relationship between science and religion, exploring the complex history and nuances that have shaped our understanding of the world. To better grasp the context, please refer to the introductory piece, which provides a comprehensive overview of the series.

A Brief History of the Convergence of Science and Faith

Let's take a brief excursion through time to examine the evolution of the relationship between science and religion.

For a detailed timeline, please click on the links provided in this article. I have also included additional information on the subject in a separate piece and made notes on it here.

The Bible plays a significant role in many religious traditions, but it is not the sole representative of religious culture. The Hebrew Bible, which is the Old Testament for Christians, is a fundamental text that has shaped the course of Jewish and Christian history. However, it is essential to recognize that the Bible is not the sole authority in religious culture, and its interpretation can vary greatly among believers.

The relationship between science and religion is a multifaceted story that is both complex and crucial, as it reveals our deep connection to one another and the world around us.

Origins of the Convergence of Science and Faith

In the early stages of human history, science and religion may have been intertwined. Charles Darwin proposed in his book Science and Religious Belief (1938) that humans evolved to be religious as a species. He believed that religion was an innate aspect of human nature, evolving alongside the development of the human brain.

As scientific evidence emerged, Darwin's views on religion began to shift. He eventually came to view religion as a product of human psychology rather than a reflection of a universal reality.

However, his grandson, Sam, proposed the theory of punctuated equilibrium, which suggested that humans evolved to be religious as a result of the concept of punctuated equilibrium. According to this theory, organisms produce eggs and sperm, and when only one is allowed to reproduce offspring, the species stops producing its own eggs and sperm.

The Evolution of Human Faith

A recent article by Harvard Law Professor Lawrence Lessig, published in the Wall Street Journal, claims that politicians from both parties are violating election laws to create a system where wealthy donors can contribute unlimited amounts while maintaining anonymity.

Lessig argues that the First Amendment should limit the influence of large donors on elections, as a system that rewards a few influential donors over working citizens is a violation of the First Amendment.

Lessig is not alone in calling for change. In October, Senate Majority Leader Harry Reid introduced the DISCLOSE Act, aimed at curbing dark money. Lessig also emphasizes the importance of holding candidates accountable to the public, whose voices cannot be silenced by large donations.

Lessig's group, Citizens for Responsibility and Ethics in Washington, filed an ethics complaint with the Campaign Finance Institute, accusing Sen. Bernie Sanders of breaking campaign finance laws.

The complaint alleges that Sanders' campaign received a $2,700 donation from an anonymous supporter during an event with Americans for Campaign Reform. Although the donation was reported on the Federal Election Commission's website, the campaign was not required to pay taxes on it.

Campaigns can accept donations of any size, but the FEC defines gifts larger than $200 as "gifts" due to their nature as a "present." Candidates can also be reimbursed for payments made during a campaign.

While Lessig is correct that a system where money from wealthy donors or corporations can be used to purchase influence does not deserve a First Amendment endorsement, it is clear that the current system is a clear violation of the law.

However, Lessig's article omits the fact that campaign finance laws do not only protect the wealthy. These laws require disclosure of donors to candidates and parties, as well as super PACs, which are not subject to contribution limits.

CREW's complaint also highlights that both Bernie Sanders and Donald Trump receive large amounts of small donations, which is legal. Lessig's article also fails to mention that Donald Trump's campaign does not have donation limits, likely due to primary contest fundraising and large donations from other donors.

Lessig's argument could be used against him. If he is successful in filing an ethics complaint, he could be held legally liable if he continues to break federal election laws.

The complaint against Sanders was filed on behalf of more than 200 organizations, including Democracy 21, Public Citizen, Public Citizen's Congress Watch, The Leadership Conference on Civil and Human Rights, and Public Citizen.

The Swiss public utility EDP, which controls the mine, has requested that the Swiss Federal Nuclear Supervisory Authority (BNZ) investigate the matter.

The Swiss Federal Nuclear Supervisory Authority has confirmed the issue, but stated that it has not yet taken any action. Federal law in Switzerland requires energy-intensive mining operations to have a general licence, and an informal one if the work is conducted on an industrial site. The company operating the uranium mine, Jura Minerals, is registered by Swiss law to a company called Jura-Prospectum.

According to EDP, it is not legally possible to carry out work at the uranium mine except under a general licence, or under an informal one if there is no work at the site. If an informal licence is not granted, a work permit is required. The Swiss radiation institute, Swiss Nuclear Research Institute SINTEF, believes that this is the only way to avoid a health catastrophe.

The Swiss newspaper Tages-Anzeiger reported that EDP had not received permission from the federal state government for EDP to have its own inspector at the mine. Swiss Radio reported that Jura-Prospectum had never received a work permit for the uranium mine. The mine is currently in a legal limbo. A representative of the mine said it is in negotiations with the federal government to resolve its regulatory situation. The company has also hired a Swiss law firm to help address regulatory issues.

According to the Tages-Anzeiger article, if Jura is found to be conducting informal mine work as not legally allowed by its licence, a formal proceeding against the nuclear authority would open.

Jura is owned by another Swiss company called Jura Mineraurs Inc. It operates the uranium mine from the outside, supplying electricity to the national grid from the mine's diesel generators.

When Swiss-based UBS-Vontobel bought Uranium One, a mining and processing company with interests in Kazakhstan, it was reported that uranium mining companies would not be allowed to operate without a licence. In order to obtain a licence, companies would have to prove a significant safety risk had emerged under the company's management.

EDP has defended its actions, stating that the mining industry must be regulated in accordance with Basler's guidelines. It is always a risk that a company operates the mine without a formal licence, according to EDP's technical director, Dr. Christoph Vondracke.

The mining and uranium mining sector may soon experience an uncertain ending. A series of recent lawsuits has been filed against the Basler agency by mining companies. The lawsuit alleges that Basler is not applying the existing regulations in the mining industry. As for Basler, its current director general, Frank-Jürgen Fels, has said that the Basler agency is prepared to take on the suits, but the regulator is also aware of the possibility that the lawsuits could be resolved.

Jura's mine and its regulatory problems have not helped, nor has the lawsuit from Vondracke against Basler.

I stumbled upon this enchanting recipe from a charming blog, and it's perfect for a Christmas dessert. It's surprisingly easy to prepare and can be stored in the freezer for up to three months!

Categories: Sweet Delights

Serves: 6-8


The most wonderful vegan Christmas treats

Ingredients for the Magical Pudding

2/3 cup of crunchy cashews

1/4 cup of creamy peanut butter

1/2 cup of sweet agave nectar or maple syrup, with a preference for maple syrup

1 1/2 teaspoons of vanilla essence

3/4 teaspoon of salt

For the Whipped Cream:

1 cup of cashews

1/2 cup of unsweetened coconut flakes

1/2 cup of maple syrup, unsweetened preferred

1/2 cup of cocoa powder, preferred

A pinch of salt

1/2 cup of heavy whipping cream

For the Vanilla Gel:

1/2 cup of unsweetened coconut flakes

1/4 cup of vanilla bean paste

1/4 cup of maple syrup, unsweetened preferred

A pinch of salt

The Process

1. Grind the cashews and peanuts in a spice grinder or coffee grinder. You can also use a food processor.

2. Blend the nuts and liquids, except the vanilla, until they're well combined.

3. Add the vanilla and salt. Blend again.

4. Add 1/2 cup of the whipped cream (if using) and mix well.

5. In another bowl, mix the coconut, heavy whipping cream, and cocoa to form a paste. Place the cashew paste and coconut cream mixture in the fridge to set, then start whipping the cream until it reaches the desired consistency. This will take a few minutes. Whip until it's light and fluffy.

6. Pour the heavy cream into your pudding bowl, using a silicone spatula. Add the remaining whipped cream and the optional vanilla.

7. Pour the mixture into greased 8-inch by 8-inch cake pans and bake at 350 degrees F for 45 minutes or until a tester comes out clean. For more chocolate pudding ideas, visit our dessert guide for vegan chocolate desserts.

8. Remove from the oven. Let cool completely, then break apart, serve, and enjoy!

A more effective approach would be to inform consumers about potential issues without requiring their involvement. The bill proposes a standard complaint form at the point of sale, providing consumers with essential information for review.

Imagine a scenario where servers note the restaurant's name, your credit card information, and a summary of your purchase. On the other end, the server should note if the order was made with an expired credit card or if the transaction was suspicious.

In the world of technology, there are devices that can support specific functions and operating systems. These devices are known as universal carriers (UCs). UCs provide a common interface that allows any device running one of several well-supported operating systems to operate on a carrier network.

A UC is simply a device that has a common hardware connection to a carrier network in order to access the service it provides. As carrier networks become more widespread and convenient, some companies and operators are offering UCs that can work with multiple devices.

One of the most common types of UCs are the PDU (Phone Distribution Unit) which allow phones to work on different networks using the same hardware and software. Others include the RSM (Rural Mobile Subscriber Line) which allows subscribers to access their rural or other service carrier phone line from any location, and the PBX (Point-to-Point Link) which allows phones to serve different carriers using a single box.

All of these types of UCs share one thing in common - the carrier network that the carrier is willing to provide. Some carriers are willing to provide access to their network, even if an iPhone doesn't fit the mold of being able to use it like it would on their network. Others want more control, and some are still waiting for Apple to decide which network is the right one for their particular network.

It is important to note though, you don't have to have a network carrier to do cellular calls through a UC.

Apple has released their operating system, iOS, for use on their iPhone and iPad. This allows any iPhone, iPad or iPod Touch running with iOS to connect to any carrier carrier.

For more information on what that means, you can go to this iPhone or iPad user guide. Here's a rundown of all the types of UCs that have been created or that Apple has provided for use with existing carriers:

PDU, or phone distribution units. Basically, you connect your iPhone to a phone distribution unit that has the software you want on it. They are generally used for small and medium businesses. PDU devices also allow you to use voice-over-IP-IP (VoIP) with your iPhone.

RSM which is a type of mobile subscriber line, or MST (Mobile Subscriber Line). These units can be used by rural or other subscriber line areas to provide voice, data or video service.

PBX which also works with the same cellular equipment, but works for businesses. It allows businesses to place voice calls directly to phone number, either a landline or a mobile.

PBX + UMTS or MMS (Multimedia Modem Telephone Line). Allows phones to connect to a phone distribution unit (PDU) that has a UMTS (Universal Mobile Telecommunications System) modem in addition to a UMTS (Universal Mobile Telecommunications System) cellular radio.

PBX + LTE (Local Area Network) to provide cellular voice service.

The notion of a peaceful passing with loved ones by one's side often conjures up images of a serene environment. Hospice facilities worldwide provide a haven for those nearing the end of life, offering a sense of comfort and support. In the United States and other developed countries, hospice centers allocate between 20% and 40% of their resources to caring for patients who can no longer bear the burden of their illness. As a relatively new practice in the US, hospice has become a valuable option for those with limited alternatives.

At their core, hospice centers strive to heal patients, providing a sense of peace and comfort during their final days. When patients are unable to leave the hospital, hospice becomes their sole option, a reality that fills me with a deep sense of empathy. Every time I must inform a patient that their final days are approaching, I am acutely aware of the weight of my decision.

Patients often make this choice due to overwhelming emotions, which can leave them feeling trapped and helpless. I, too, have experienced this feeling, but I have learned to manage it by taking short walks outside to clear my mind and regain a sense of empowerment. This newfound perspective allows me to better support those I love during difficult times.

On the other hand, I am also aware of the emotional toll that comes with watching loved ones deteriorate. It can be a heavy burden to bear, and it's easy to feel like life is a cruel joke. However, by shifting my focus away from the end and toward the present moment, I am able to find a new sense of purpose.

When patients leave the hospital after an extended stay, they often experience a profound sense of loss. The pain and suffering they endure can be unbearable, and it's natural to feel a sense of pain alongside them. Yet, as we return to our daily lives, we often forget this feeling, leaving our families and friends overwhelmed by the emotional complexity of hospital stays.

Hospice centers exist to ease the pain of the end-of-life experience for patients who would otherwise be alone in their grief. In addition to receiving care from a dedicated team, patients often have the opportunity to reconnect with loved ones who may have fallen by the wayside. Hospice programs are staffed with specially trained professionals who facilitate the process and assist patients with their final wishes and activities.

In recent decades, hospitals have evolved to offer more personalized care to patients in their final weeks and months, making the end-of-life transition easier and more natural. Hospice has adapted accordingly, aiming to provide seamless care to patients and their families.

Hospice centers offer patients a range of support services during their final months, including:

* Information about their medical history and prognosis for their loved ones
* A dedicated support person to ask questions and seek guidance

We also provide an array of support services for patients as they approach the end of life, including guidance from nurses, medical staff, and patient advocates. If patients require additional support or assistance, there are dedicated programs available that offer confidential counseling, physical comfort, and other services to patients and their families.

There are many reasons why patients may choose to remain in the hospital until the end of life. Some may be unable to afford the costs, while others prefer to make medical decisions for their loved ones. Additionally, hospitals are required by federal and state laws to provide hospice care, offering comfort and support to end-of-life patients. However, there are also patients who must remain in the hospital due to complex medical conditions, and hospitals are required to provide them with pain relief and hospice care. For these patients, hospice care is a vital component of their treatment.

Whimsical contraptions, known as "punched cards," were once a popular method for storing and processing information within early calculating machines. These curious devices were fashioned from cardboard or paper and featured intricate patterns of perforations, which served as a unique means of conveying data.

During the 1950s and 1960s, punched cards were the primary means of data storage, preceding the advent of more sophisticated storage technologies such as magnetic tape and disk storage. To process the information encoded on these cards, a computer would meticulously read the sequence of perforations and execute the corresponding calculations or instructions.

Punched cards found widespread application across various domains, including scientific inquiry, commercial data processing, and government record-keeping. Moreover, they were also utilized for programming early computers, as the perforations on the cards could be leveraged to represent instructions in a machine-readable format.

Regrettably, punched cards have since been supplanted by more efficient and convenient storage and processing technologies, rendering them an antiquated relic of a bygone era.

A delicious dish requires the following components:

- 9 lasagna noodle sheets
- 2 ½ cups of ricotta cheese
- 2 cups of spinach, thawed and drained
- 2 cups of cooked vegetables (such as diced bell peppers, mushrooms, zucchini, and/or onions)
- 1 ½ cups of marinara sauce
- 1 ½ cups of mozzarella cheese
- ½ cup of parmesan cheese
- 2 tablespoons of fresh herbs (such as basil, oregano, and/or parsley)
- Salt and ground black pepper, to taste

To prepare this dish, follow these steps:

1. Preheat the oven to 350°F. Grease a 9x13-inch baking dish.
2. In a medium bowl, combine the ricotta, spinach, cooked vegetables, 1 cup of marinara sauce, 1 cup of mozzarella cheese, herbs, salt, and pepper.
3. Spread ½ cup of marinara sauce over the bottom of the dish.
4. Place 3 noodles over the sauce and spread evenly with half of the ricotta mixture.
5. Top with ½ cup of mozzarella cheese and another ½ cup of marinara sauce.
6. Repeat layering with 3 more noodles, the remaining ricotta mixture, and ½ cup of mozzarella cheese.
7. Place the last 3 noodles on top and spread the remaining sauce over them and sprinkle with parmesan cheese.
8. Bake for 30 minutes, then cover with foil and bake for an additional 15 minutes, or until the noodles are tender.
9. Let the dish cool for 10 minutes before serving. Enjoy!

The American Civil Liberties Union initiated a legal action on Wednesday to compel the Justice Department to divulge which federal entities have received federal funding to monitor protests against the presidency of Donald Trump, an action that civil liberties advocates argue would benefit Trump's critics.

The lawsuit, filed in the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia by the ACLU and the National Lawyers Guild, represents the latest effort by civil liberties and civil rights organizations to ensure that the Trump administration adheres to Trump's campaign promises on illegal immigration.

The Justice Department failed to respond to The Washington Times' inquiry for comment on the lawsuit, but Trump has consistently criticized the federal government for not taking sufficient measures to secure the nation's southern border, which he promised to achieve with a "real and effective" wall and significant budget cuts.

The ACLU filed its lawsuit, claiming that the administration cannot hide behind federal funding limitations to refuse information about which "federal entities" are participating in such monitoring programs.

The lawsuit requests a federal judge to order the government to disclose which of its divisions currently engage in surveillance activities.

The ACLU's national legal director, Anthony D. Romero, noted that he first introduced the Freedom of Information Act in 1980 to compel the release of classified documents from the Reagan administration because the administration had refused to accept his request for the documents as a Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) request.

"It is an historic abuse of power by the Trump administration that has no legal basis but is instead motivated by hostility, fear, and a desire to evade the public's right to learn what the U.S. government is doing," Romero said. "We are asking for a return to the FOIA, and to make clear that federal entities need to disclose details of all secret surveillance programs so the public can know what they are up to."

The DOJ, meanwhile, has asked that the lawsuit be dismissed.

The ACLU's lawsuit follows a letter it sent to the DOJ and the FBI yesterday to alert them "we would be filing this lawsuit should the government fail to meet its responsibilities under law," Romero said. The DOJ, the ACLU said, needs to "make clear that federal entities that participate in programs to surveil people or groups must follow the law in doing so."

The Freedom of Information Act currently prevents the government from releasing essential information about its activities. The federal government is required to reveal information about its surveillance activities to the public as well as to Congress if they have information related to national security.

The administration continues to fight that disclosure, particularly following Trump's claim that 3 million to 5 million illegal votes were cast in the 2016 presidential election — an assertion that the DOJ has said was "without credible evidence."

I was still on probation and trying to stay clean, but I just couldn't resist the urge. I would go out and drink every month or so, and eventually, I would go back to my old ways. The United States has witnessed a significant decline in the number of individuals who engage in the consumption of a certain plant-based substance over the past decade. This figure represents a substantial decrease from the estimated 16% in 2006 and 22% in 2011.

The data collected by the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Administration highlights the effectiveness of a more cautious and controlled approach to the substance, which has been stigmatized for many years. The National Health and Nutrition Examination Study, conducted by the National Center for Health Statistics in September, reported that approximately 1 in 5 U.S. adults has used this substance.

The researchers cautioned that it is too early to determine whether the downward trend in marijuana use among Americans is due to changes in public opinion or other factors. Dr. Sidney T. Wolfe, chief of the U.S. National Institute on Drug Abuse, noted that the findings may be linked to a decrease in cigarette smoking and a shift in the survey's demographics, with a larger sample of people over age 50.

Among recent users, 13.8% reported their current consumption levels were "not bad," compared to 22.1% in 2006 and 29.9% in 2010. Of those who had used the substance more recently, 35.2% expressed "great concern" about it, compared to 9.2% in 2006 and 13.2% in 2010.

Wolfe emphasized that the figures in the new data indicate that marijuana use is still not considered high-risk, as the potential for harmful effects is not taken into account.

Michael Warner, director of marijuana research and policy at the drug policy reform group Smart Approaches to Marijuana, stated that the government data demonstrates that when marijuana was legalized in Colorado and Washington state, it led to a significant public health benefit in reducing the harms associated with drug use and addiction.

Warner noted that when marijuana use was restricted, the public health gains did not necessarily outweigh the damage done by marijuana use. He emphasized that the government's new data do not suggest that marijuana is not a problem but rather that it is a problem in a different category.

"It's better not to give it away, but it's even better when it is regulated," Warner said.

The letter was sent to the White House counsel, Kathryn Warner, and the director of national intelligence, Elliot Thompson.

"As you're aware, the United States conducts targeted killings on a regular basis, and the administration has established rules to authorize this type of targeted killing that have been widely praised by advocates of human rights and civil liberties," Flynn continued. "However, in response to public concerns over the administration's legal authority, the administration has been proposing new legal justifications for targeted killings that could raise serious constitutional issues. We're asking the Department of Justice to review and, if necessary, reject the proposed changes that might further erode the principle of accountability and transparency that's essential to our democratic system."

In previous conversations with The New York Times, administration officials said the proposed rule changes aim to assure the privacy community and international partners that U.S. authorities will follow the same rules in the event of a drone strike that kills a U.S. citizen. If the strike kills a noncitizen, they will be subject to "proper procedures," said an official in the White House speaking on condition of anonymity.

In 2011, the foundation released a report finding that the government had been conducting secret lethal drone strikes in Pakistan.

On Friday morning, a reporter asked the president about Jaxon Flynn's recommendation in a press briefing, to which the president replied that he hadn't seen the letter. The president said he would look into the issue, mentioning "legitimate concerns" in the past "but I think they've been addressed through increased transparency and our own procedures."

Earlier this week, the Department of Justice wrote to the foundation seeking a formal investigation of the group's claims on drone use.

Greetings from the sun-kissed shores of New Jersey, where the 2017 Summer Camp of America is now underway. As you may not be the star of these summer camp musicals, let me share with you the fascinating process behind their creation.

The show begins with a brief introduction featuring a character from the past, who may reappear later in the performance. This character is often the main protagonist from an original work, but not based on real-life events. This is the first time this character appears in this specific show, with an updated version each time.

Five characters, all designed by Bill Watterson, are the foundation of the story. These characters were first published in newspapers and later became one of the most successful syndicated strips of all time.

The main characters then embark on a journey through various popular musicals, including "Happiest Days Of Our Lives," "Roxanne," "Swan Lake," "The Last Five Years," "A Whole New World," "The Hearsay Tales Of Bea Arthur," and "Singing In The Rain." Each story features a protagonist sent to a camp to learn and grow, often from a young age. They face challenges and experience new things, including long car rides.

The story diverges from traditional camp tales by incorporating music, music festivals, and performances to drive character development. Some events occur before the camp, and music is used to heighten emotions, making the characters feel like they're transported to these moments.

I'm thrilled to share my enthusiasm for coconut with you all. My love affair with coconuts began around six years ago, and since then, I've been exploring various ways to incorporate it into my daily life. While some coconut recipes may not be as impressive as others, I've found that certain ones truly stand out. Take coconut cake, for instance - it's a game-changer! My advice to fellow food enthusiasts is to give this cake a try. To achieve the perfect coconut cake, it's essential to use high-quality coconut that's at least semi-ripe. When in doubt, opt for the best. When preparing the cake, ensure you're using semi-ripe coconut creamers, avoiding the bitter and unripe ones. Then, cook the coconut in batches until it's easy to crumble into flour. If you don't have coconut flour, you can substitute it with rice flour. Keep in mind that coconut flour has a light consistency and is relatively high in calories, so it's a good idea to limit the amount used in this recipe. If needed, add a little more coconut flour to balance the flavors. This cake recipe requires refrigeration for at least two hours before serving.

Yield: 12-15 servings

Vegan, Vegetarian, and Gluten-Free Chocolate Cake Recipe

Ingredients:

Coconut: 1/2 medium

Eggs: 1 large

Coconut oil: 1 tablespoon

Olive oil: 3 tablespoons

Flour: 1 cup

Vanilla extract: 1 teaspoon

Lemon zest: 1/2 lemon

Chocolate chips: about 1/2 cup

Instructions:

Preheat your oven to 300 degrees. In a medium-sized bowl, combine the coconut, eggs, and coconut oil. Gradually add 3/4 cup of flour, adjusting the consistency as needed. Mix well. Slowly incorporate the remaining 2/3 cup coconut flour and the remaining 3/4 cup coconut flour, alternating them evenly. Scrape down the sides as necessary. Gently fold in the cocoa powder, vanilla extract, lemon zest, and chocolate chips.

Bake until a toothpick inserted comes out clean, approximately 35-40 minutes.

Cool for a few minutes on a wire rack before removing from the pan.

Serve and enjoy!

Note: This cake is vegan, vegetarian, and gluten-free.

A federal court on Wednesday rendered a permanent decision regarding a significant component of President Donald Trump's immigration policy. The ruling affects the enforcement of a policy that would have allowed the deportation of up to 4 million individuals living in the US without proper documentation.

The ban on entry from seven countries, introduced in late January, triggered widespread protests and chaos at airports across the country. The travel restriction was temporarily halted by a federal judge in Portland, Oregon, following a lawsuit filed by Washington state and Minnesota, who argued that the policy aimed to discriminate against individuals based on their religious beliefs.

President Trump has reaffirmed his commitment to upholding the ban.

A three-judge panel determined that the travel ban was unconstitutional due to its arbitrary nature, lack of evidence, and violation of the separation of powers. The judges also found that the government failed to demonstrate the legitimacy of its concerns.

The ruling impacts two sections of the executive order. One provision, which applies to citizens of Iran, Iraq, Libya, Somalia, Sudan, Syria, and Yemen, includes an indefinite ban on entry for individuals from these countries who do not already possess a visa. The other provision, affecting all refugees, extends a 120-day ban on travel to the US for individuals from Syria, Iraq, Iran, Libya, Somalia, Sudan, Syria, or Yemen.

The Supreme Court declined to reinstate the travel ban on Monday evening.

"The president has issued an executive order; that executive order is currently suspended," the Department of Homeland Security stated on Wednesday.

The ban was set to expire on March 12. Following the court's ruling, the administration announced that the ban would be reinstated on March 10. According to government officials, the ban will take effect at 8:59 p.m. local time (5:59 p.m. ET) on Sunday, March 10.

The Department of Justice and State Department could not be immediately reached for comment, and the White House also did not comment.

In a statement, the American Civil Liberties Union expressed disagreement with the ruling, stating that President Trump "cannot rewrite immigration law on a whim and expect the Supreme Court to stand by it."

"[The judge] correctly pointed out that the federal government does not have the authority to ban immigration based on nationality," ACLU Executive Director Anthony Romero said. "President Trump's executive order violates that principle."

On Wednesday, the Trump administration filed an appeal with the Supreme Court, seeking permission to defend the travel ban with a narrower argument.

The Supreme Court has heard oral arguments in a closely-watched case regarding the travel ban. The case challenges President Trump's executive order, issued while he was in office, which bans individuals from Iran, Libya, Somalia, Sudan, Syria, and Yemen with visas or refugee status. The Supreme Court announced on April 12 that it will take up the case of refugees, who are not subject to the ban.

Meanwhile, the Department of Justice has filed a new motion to overturn lower court rulings that temporarily halted the travel ban. The court will have a new date – March 10 – to rule on the ban.

We should revise the term "liquefied" and "diesel" to "diesel energy." Instead of utilizing "hydrogen," "clean coal" and "green energy" to refer to energy technologies that produce energy without greenhouse gases, we should use these terms only when they are not part of an alternative energy source called "diesel."

While the term "diesel" is often associated with cars that run on diesel fuel -- which is the most carbon-intensive fuel -- the energy technologies that can aid us in replacing fossil fuels with cleaner energy could benefit the majority of people, including those who do not drive cars, such as solar panels and windpower generators.

"In many regions around the world, where we already have a substantial amount of solar power, we simply do not require a significant amount of electricity generated from diesel," says Kevin Bales, president of The Brookings Institution Energy Institute. He states that's because it is possible to install sufficient panels and turbines to meet most of the grid's demand of electricity from renewable sources without utilizing diesel.

However, how could we determine the precise amount of energy we require to cover all of our needs with clean energy in the future -- especially when there are numerous different types of energy systems? Bales asserts that researchers have developed technology that can measure the amount of energy that individual technologies can deliver at various points on the supply chain.

If it costs more to procure energy from "hydrogen" or "diesel," we should compensate accordingly. By contrast, more efficient fuels would likely save consumers money, and cleaner fuels would also make our energy system less susceptible to shortages or disruptions to the power grid.

"That's a significant factor in terms of conserving energy and avoiding costs on fuel," says Mark Siegel, an economist and energy expert at Harvard. "That's when you utilize more renewables, not when you invest in an alternative energy source."

For instance, the cost of renewables is decreasing, but the cost of alternative energy technologies, such as nuclear energy, is increasing. In a recent report, the U.S. Energy Information Agency reported that alternative energy sources may have a more limited role in the U.S. for the foreseeable future than renewable fuels, meaning that their share of U.S. energy production will decline in the decades ahead.

"The primary objective of the alternative fuels is they are less dependable than clean energy," says Bales. "I prefer clean energy, but when you are discussing alternative fuel sources, you are discussing technologies that are much less dependable than clean energy."

In contrast, clean energy could be utilized whenever and wherever we have energy sources, including on the grid. If a grid outage necessitates 100,000 gallons of diesel fuel to power a home, it can make sense to utilize 100,000 gallons of biodiesel or another alternative energy source to make up that energy gap. If we are discussing a country that imports oil from a stable country in Asia instead of relying on the unstable prices of oil in the international market for domestic energy, we should utilize 100,000 gallons of clean energy.

We may not be able to halt climate change or even the current rise of environmental threats like climate change. However, we can contribute to environmental preservation by adopting clean energy alternatives. If we could transition to technologies that utilize electricity more efficiently, utilize more clean energy on the grid, and save money by switching to biodiesel, wind turbines and solar panels, the world will be safer, healthier and richer as a result.

The role of the gut microbiota in maintaining the intestinal barrier and producing host mucin molecules has been recently identified. However, less is known about their role in regulating the development of the host immune system. The composition of the intestinal microbiota in an adult is not yet clear in normal immune development of the intestinal epithelium. Therefore, we conducted a meta-analysis of 7 studies reporting fecal samples in a controlled environment. We found no significant differences in fecal bacterial samples in healthy men and women after a 4-hour antibiotic pulse. However, we identified significant differences among fecal bacterial groups in intestinal mucosal cells of healthy humans and mice. Additionally, we found a significant difference between fecal bacterial groups in mucus from intestinal epithelial cells of healthy humans and mice. Our results suggest that fecal bacteria may contribute to the development of the intestinal mucosa.

Bacteria are a common feature in the fecal microbiota, although differences have been reported between healthy and immunocompromised humans. In humans, the intestinal microbiota can be colonized by many species without changing its composition. However, with some bacteria, there may be an important change in intestinal microbiota in immunocompetent or elderly subjects. The development and differentiation of the intestinal mucosa are highly dependent on the resident community of the microbiota. A role of the microbiota in the development of the intestinal mucosa has been demonstrated in several investigations.

The art of persuasion is crucial in horror cinema. The ability to distract the viewer from the absurdity of a situation can make a movie more believable. For instance, a film can make the viewer believe that a ordinary event is actually a crucial plot point, or that a character is not what they seem.

However, this technique can also backfire and make the movie less scary. When the audience becomes too invested in the story, they may start to question the logic of the events unfolding before their eyes. This can lead to a loss of tension and ultimately, a decrease in fear.

While this is not necessarily a bad thing, it does depend on the goal of the movie. A good horror film should aim to frighten and unsettle the viewer. However, a great horror movie can still be effective without relying on suspension of disbelief.

There are certain situations where suspension of disbelief is not necessary. For example, a horror movie set in a world without magic or supernatural elements. In these cases, the film can focus on the real-world terrors that people face.

In more abstract cases, such as an alien invasion or a mind-control scenario, suspension of disbelief may be necessary. However, the audience may still be able to connect with the emotions and themes of the film, even if they don't fully believe in the events.

A good horror film should use suspension of disbelief to take the viewer on a journey of fear and unease. It should push the boundaries of what is acceptable and make the viewer question what is real and what is not.

When the participants were given the opportunity to decline any of the feedback they received, the participants who received the most unwanted feedback in this way tended to make less accurate, fewer productive decisions than those who had received less negative feedback.

The researchers found that individuals in groups can make decisions together that they wouldn't make for themselves, and in doing so, can alter the actions of others. In other words, the dynamics within real-life groups are influenced by what occurs behind the scenes, rather than on the surface.

According to Israeli legislation, these individuals could be required to sign a declaration stating that they have no intention of becoming citizens of a Jewish state. The court determined that Israel has the authority to refuse such a declaration.

If a European country demands an Italian to declare themselves a citizen of another European state, why not a Palestinian or an Algerian?

The court has not yet issued a final decision on the case, which has raised numerous questions for the international community.

Suad, a 15-year-old girl, was forced to sign a declaration when she arrived in Israel in 1961 to study. At the time, she was only permitted to enter and leave the country with a passport containing only her mother's name and birth certificate.

"There were no such requirements when I was coming here, nor when I grew up," she says. Suad had to leave Saudi Arabia for Egypt due to her father being a Saudi citizen, and after an extensive search, she was able to obtain a new passport with her mother's name. The change was not a problem for her as she had also been registered as a Saudi citizen. However, her father was not as fortunate.

"His citizenship was taken away, and they took everything from him," Suad recounts.

Suad was then forced to take the oath in a special room at the airport. She is now an Israeli citizen and enjoys the same rights as other citizens. "It's not a difficult decision to make, especially for me, because I never believed in this decision," she says.

In 2011, a young Palestinian man, Hani Abu-Dayyeh, was arrested by Israeli authorities for participating in protests against the military occupation and occupation of the Al-Aqsa Mosque compound. He was held without charge for two years and then detained for five years in the notorious Ayalon prison, where he witnessed interrogations, torture, and forced confessions from fellow inmates. He was released on bail in 2009 and took part in several nonviolent protests in his hometown of Nablus.

According to Palestinian law, Abu-Dayyeh had to recognize Israel as the state of the Jewish people and declare support for its presence in that holy site. However, the decision did not affect Abu-Dayyeh's status as an Israeli citizen, and he was never required to take an oath of loyalty to the state.

It's a serious violation of Israeli citizens' rights. How can they refuse an EU declaration of non-participation in a Jewish state?

Hanan Ashrawi, head of the Palestine Liberation Organization Institute of National Security and Intelligence at Tel Aviv University, believes the ECJ was incorrect in its ruling in Israel's favor. When a person voluntarily comes to Israel for a short period of time for study and employment, as Suad's mother did, the decision should be made after that fact.

However, when a person becomes a permanent resident to work or have a family, Israel does not need an EU declaration.

Ashrawi says European countries should respect the decisions of individual states and treat non-participation in a Jewish state as a privilege based on the person's personal status. "This should not be a condition under which Israel is forced to treat EU citizens with suspicion and harassment," she says.

In addition to European institutions, Suad and Abu-Dayyeh were supported by the international community when they were fighting the matter. The European Parliament stated that a European citizen in no circumstances has any rights to refuse to go to Israel. In 2011, the United Kingdom, France, Sweden, and many countries in Europe and North America also expressed support for Suad and Abu-Dayyeh.

The ECJ noted that the Israeli law requiring an Italian to sign a declaration made it possible to deny any European a residency permit without his consent.

But Ashrawi believes the ECJ has not gone far enough. There is no requirement for a European to declare themselves a citizen of another European country.

A man of rare courage has emerged in the world of motor sports. Sebastian Vettel, the world champion, has shown the field that when men step out of fear, they can turn it into an advantage. In his first year as world champion, he was the one who fought back, and now he is a man who is still trying to fight back.

He has proven over the year that when he faces fear, he turns around and makes it his advantage. He has shown that no one can beat him, and he will be more dangerous than anyone else. He is the only one who can challenge his Mercedes team-mate, Nico Rosberg. And when Rosberg is at his best, you need him as much as anyone else does.

Sebastian Vettel is a man who has consistently beaten Rosberg, winning the world title six times. He was closest to the title in 2014, but Rosberg did not come back from a bad start. Vettel was there to beat him whenever Rosberg got in trouble, winning all four of those titles with a better rate of success than anyone else.

The same is true of 2015. Rosberg missed the first half of the season and finished behind Vettel four times, four times he finished ahead. In the second half, Vettel outqualified Rosberg in races. Vettel will be there to beat Rosberg whenever he gets in trouble, winning all four of those titles with a better rate of success than anyone else.

It is worth remembering that Vettel is a man who has never been beaten by a fellow driver in a race that was contested with both cars on track. He never had a chance against Lewis Hamilton. He is never going to beat Kimi Raikkonen because there weren't enough points available to him in qualifying races.

There is a strong case to be made that for every point scored by Vettel in 2016, he has lost around seven to Raikkonen. In a race such as Singapore, you need to lose around 15-30 places just to get around the point spread. Vettel may well only lose two points and Raikkonen one or two.

That should not be at all surprising. The difference between how they drive has never been so great. Raikkonen has been faster than Vettel in every race this year, and Vettel has been quicker than Raikkonen in every race last year. What difference in terms of lap times makes? It is a big difference.

The difference between the men is a big difference. The gap was as wide as the difference between the top two in the points table in 2015, and then the gap widened considerably. The other difference between them lies in performance. Vettel has been faster. Raikkonen has been more consistent. They are both fast.

The biggest difference between the pair is undoubtedly their driving styles. Vettel and Raikkonen drive very differently. Their styles are very different. The difference between the pace of Vettel and Raikkonen in any particular race has depended heavily on the weather and whether or not they are taking advantage of conditions that they could be in better conditions – not at all different from what we saw in 2015, of course.

But Vettel has proven by sheer force of will to be more of a risk-taker than anyone else has shown in many years. Raikkonen – and Ferrari – have no experience of a man like Vettel in a team. A team with so many championship contenders with so many championships to claim over a career could not cope with an opponent like Vettel at their peak.

What Raikkonen learned is that the car doesn't matter in a fight at the top of the sport. The car needs to be better, the driver needs to be better.

If you are as good as Vettel at taking risks, you will always be faster. You will always be able to be in a better position than your peers.

Republicans also want to end government rules against blocking websites, which they say gives rise to online piracy. They're seeking congressional oversight of the rules created by the FCC, which may not be a popular move within the tech sector.

This research was conducted within the framework of a comprehensive study on household consumption patterns. A nationwide survey of US families with children was conducted, gathering information on daily food intake, portion sizes, and frequency of consumption. The survey utilized a 3-day food frequency questionnaire to assess the quality and quantity of foods consumed, as well as the overall food system. The primary goal was to examine the differences in portion sizes and energy density between high- and low-income households, with a focus on estimating the energy cost of production. Additionally, the study aimed to evaluate the impact of food labeling regulations on school meal patterns, building upon the 1998 National Healthy School Food Policy.

PROCEDURES:

The findings presented are based on 10,542 interviews with low-income children and their mothers, conducted over a 30-day period in November 2008. The results showed that children from high-income households consumed an average of 11.0% more total energy compared to children from low-income households (P =.015). Adjustments were made for factors such as child age, sex, race/ethnicity, socio-economic status, and number of meals consumed daily. Furthermore, the energy cost per serving was found to be 2.2 times higher in high-income households compared to low-income households, leading to a decrease in energy intake among children in both groups (P<.001).

CONCLUSION:

These findings suggest that providing accurate and meaningful information about food energy values to parents, as well as offering healthy and energy-dense options in school meal programs, may help reduce the energy cost of food for families with students.

In the beginning, I stumbled upon a peculiar documentation that left me bewildered. It was my second day of coding in Elm, and I was already perplexed. However, I quickly discovered the concept of passing a function as a parameter that accepts the first argument and the result of the computation, and it was then that the magic of composing functions began to unfold.

What is the essence of Elm's signature? What does a function with a signature that resembles this do? How can we combine a function with another function? And what is the distinction between passing a function as an argument and creating one?

Furthermore, what does it take to comprehend the true nature of a function and its actions? And why is it essential to grasp this concept?

These questions will be addressed later, but please explore the documentation of our exemplary Elm application to understand the significance of passing and composing functions and the disparity between using the library as a reference and utilizing it as a starting point for your own application.

We will delve into the function's signature, which appears as follows:

main = do f <- getArgs let res = function <$> getArgs (fun f) -- Functions which act like pure functions -> (mf. getArgs f) res

It seems that you can pass a function as an argument to some function in the following ways:

getArgs is the function's getArgs method

is the function's method getArgs = getArgs :: Functor f => f a -> f a

The function f is an inner function

is an inner function getArgs f is the function's getArgs method

is the function's method (mf. getArgs) f is the function's <$>, <*>, and >>= methods

The function f is an outer function

is the function's,, and methods f is an inner function

(mf. getArgs) f is also referred to as an inline function, meaning the function's body is the outer function.

If you are familiar with lambda calculus, you must be familiar with the functions >>= and >>

For our purposes here, the inner function >>= enables us to create the function, so we do not need to concern ourselves with it anymore.

However, the signature of our function is somewhat complicated, so we need to examine the signature of another functional programming language, Haskell.

Haskell's signature is:

main :: IO () main = do print $ (,) <$> getArgs print $ ():<*> $ getArgs print $ getArgs >>= print

The return type of the function is IO (), so it returns a value of type IO (). It also has two function's return types. The first is >>=, which takes two arguments (called arguments ), which becomes the function's result. The second function is >>, which takes a value of type IO () and an argument (called return ), which becomes the function's result

And that is it.

Now all you need to do is:

import Control.Monad import Control.Lens import Data.List main :: IO () main = do args <- getArgs print args lift $ lens (fmap >>=) (f >>=). args

The function fmap f, when applied to a list of functions, takes them and passes them to f itself. Therefore, fmap f is our function signature, and it takes a list of functions and returns itself.

Now, the function fmap f takes a function x with only one argument, x, and returns another function, which has a list of functions as its result and a result of type IO ().

The result of fmap f, as you could see above, is a function that works the same way as f, that is, it has a main method which takes a single argument, the whole current list of functions.

The Haskell signature of fmap f is:

main :: (forall k. Monad m) => m (forall f. Functor f => f a -> f a)

The forall keyword means that the function we are composing can have a return type of any type.

When we combine this with the function signature we have, we have the function signature:

main :: IO () main = do print $ (,) <$> getArgs print $ (:<*>) $ getArgs print $ getArgs >>= print lift $ lens (fmap >>=) (f >>=). args

For those who frequent our website, this news is nothing new. For those who don't, it's likely that you'll come across it as part of the usual news cycle. However, I must admit that I struggled to find any concrete information about these individuals.

I began my search by looking for English-language translations of the article, but to no avail. I had to scour the web for various translations, which I found to be somewhat unreliable. Even Wikipedia, a reliable source of information, didn't seem to have any information on the matter. The only thing I could find was some background information and photos on the Russian news site Komsomolskaya Pravda.

I did manage to find some information on Sputnik News, but what I found was somewhat perplexing. The article claimed that this was part of a larger military "information war." However, there was no evidence or facts presented to support this claim. Instead, the article focused on the supposed presence of Russian troops on the ground in Ukraine, ready to fight for Donbas. It also mentioned that the Russian military had been sending military aid to the separatists.

It's worth noting that this isn't the first time Russian soldiers have been detained in Ukraine. The article lists several recent instances where Russian soldiers have been detained by Ukrainian soldiers. It seems that these individuals are being held in Ukrainian prisons.

What's so wrong with that? It's a real war, and one that is gaining international attention. Why are these soldiers being singled out while the real war continues to unfold in Donbas and elsewhere?

It's interesting that the article, written by a Ukrainian citizen, refers to the troops as "Russian" soldiers. The article cites two videos featuring the Russian troops: one on a Russian government website and one on Vkontakte, Russia's version of Facebook.

But where are the other Russian soldiers in Ukraine? The first video shows a soldier clearly marked as being from the Russian army, but where are the others? Why don't we see any pictures of these Russian military personnel?

It's difficult to say. The Russian soldiers are identified as such, and they appear to be wearing the standard Russian military uniform. This is a common practice in Russian media, where pictures of captured soldiers appear in videos and articles. However, there is a notable absence of photos and images of Russian soldiers captured in Ukraine and being transferred to Ukrainian prisons.

In contrast, there are many reports and images of captured Ukrainian soldiers in Eastern Ukraine. It's curious that there is a lack of similar images of Russian soldiers.

That person will be standing alongside President Obama, on a platform designed to resemble the Oval Office. It appears to be tailored for a wheelchair-bound individual to access the edge.

This is one of over 300 temporary structures President Obama has transformed into the Oval Office during his five years in office. Since 2008, when he was campaigning for the presidency, he has had a different Oval Office setup each year to host a different event. It began in 2009 with the White House Correspondents' Dinner.

This year's setup marks his eighth as president.

However, not just any year. The "Presidential Oval Office" has a unique atmosphere this year, given the new occupant at the top: President Trump.

To commemorate the occasion, the White House unveiled a new photo of Obama and the president-elect in the Oval Office. In his inaugural address, Trump promised to "make America great again," and, for a moment, it seemed Americans might get an Oval Office photo.

However, when Trump took the oath on January 20, it was his predecessor, Obama, standing behind him at the podium.

For a White House with many permanent structures, it's not as though the Oval Office has been a haven for the occasional photo opportunity. This year, most of the pictures show the president with a framed photograph of himself alongside a president or president-elect from another country.

This year might be the exception.

"We see this year as one where it's less of a novelty and more of an opportunity for the administration to build upon an historic legacy and to celebrate the presidency," said White House Chief of Staff Denis McDonough.

It's also the second year in a row the Oval Office will be different over its three days, following the change in the occupant in 1993.

That change came a year shy of his impeachment trial, but on the day he was led out of the Senate's chamber, President Nixon sat on the Oval Office table, as he had almost every day in office.

The Oval Office is a space that the first couple of years in office had tried to create with a view of the White House. That changed in 2009 as the president's wife, Michelle Obama, said she "started to feel that this year, we needed to take steps to acknowledge the Oval Office in a new and meaningful way."

Since then, President Obama has turned the Oval Office into an office of creativity and art, while President Bush had it filled with desks, files, and a TV — and he didn't seem to notice. President Clinton took it over with a wall of pictures and a couch that doubled as office seating. It stayed in that setup for eight years.

And, of course, there had to be a photo opportunity in place for the first lady, who will turn her attention to the State Department on Friday.

"The president and the first lady are not averse to showing up and doing something, and we would anticipate a photo opportunity," McDonough explained.

The query that has persisted for two decades is, "When can my elders face consequences for enabling their child's excessive use of a certain plant?"

Let's delve into the specifics.

In the state of Colorado, any individual under the age of 21 can undergo a blood test at the police station, which would detect the presence of THC and its metabolites in their system, or a urine test for THC residue.

The outcome varies from person to person, and the police station's handling of the samples also differs. However, the general idea is that if the individual tests positive, they would face a two-and-a-half-month imprisonment and a $2,500 fine. For those under 21, this would mean missing school sports and paying an estimated $200 for this privilege.

The theory is that the Colorado Police Academy would educate young adults on the consequences of their actions, but that's not the case. For the past two decades, there has been no drug testing, no consequences for the youth. (I was under the impression that I had to pay my fine of $200, but the instructors were unclear about that.)

The Academy courses do not teach anything that isn't readily available online, with the exception of the "Ride to Excellence" course and a basic course on alcohol-based driving, which includes a drink or two.

On June 28, the Colorado Supreme Court ruled that this no longer had to be the case.

"While the Court finds that this is likely to have a negligible impact on law enforcement (as most defendants will plead guilty), the court acknowledges that any such impact will be very difficult to predict," the court decided. In other words, you'll just spend a few hours in jail. There isn't an ounce of the plant in your system and zero signs of impairment, which means you should be free to go home.

"We applaud the Colorado Supreme Court for recognizing that it is illegal to punish minors for the personal conduct of their elders," wrote Jim Mello of the American Civil Liberties Union in a statement.

However, it was just one judge, and the Colorado Supreme Court hasn't issued an official ruling. The police and courts have yet to decide whether this is the right message to send. And the district court judge doesn't think that was so bad.

A spokesperson for the Colorado Department of Regulatory Agencies noted that the ruling doesn't change their stance on plant arrests.

"CDA continues to oppose legalization and enforcement, and will continue to enforce existing criminal laws and to make sure that our young people are not being criminalized for using an herbal product for which they believe," said the spokesperson.

This stance remains questionable, and it's unlikely to change anytime soon.

It was at a gathering of the European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) this January, following a complaint from the food industry, that the agency first confirmed this was the case.

In its annual report published on Wednesday, EFSA reported that it was investigating "an alarming rise in the number of samples of imported fresh produce that were found to have traces of a particular banned pesticide".

Among them was apples from Germany, which were "found to have contamination to a level that, if not corrected, might make them unfit for human consumption". The apples had originally come from China.

Germany has reacted with fury. Foreign Minister Guido Westerwelle said, "This really has to be solved as soon as possible. We are extremely concerned by this situation."

The EU's food watchdog has set a deadline of March 31 to finish its investigation into a variety of imported products from China following a complaint from companies.

EFSA says the cases of contaminated apples might still be going undetected. "A number of samples … were submitted by concerned parties which have not been fully analysed by the analytical laboratories and therefore cannot be confirmed," EFSA's report said, adding that it would "continue to investigate any samples with the aim of obtaining a definitive confirmation".

Last month, France decided to ban imports of products from Chinese suppliers who produce products used to produce the highly toxic pesticide paraquat. On Thursday, Brazil followed suit by putting restrictions on the sale of Chinese food products.

"This is something the EU needs to act on immediately," says Greenpeace European food policy director Lutz Bachmann. "This is an issue that the EU has failed to address over the past 20 years. This has led to huge public concern."

According to the Food Standards Agency France (FSA), last summer the French authorities discovered a total of 23 products made using paraquat, the trade name for a pesticide banned in the EU in 2005. The FSA's report of 2012 said that of 1,800 samples of paraquat taken from France, 1,200 contained contamination, including one in 2012 that was deemed as "extremely serious".

China, says Bachmann, is guilty of exporting its pollution problems to other countries through the use of chemicals for which it is an exporter. "It's as though they want to be free of the contamination problem in France and Brazil but also want the EU to accept that this is what happens when we export to China," he says.

The problems of contaminated exports have been documented before, in the United States in 2008, when a chemical used for making plastic bottles ended up in apple juice sold in New Jersey, USA. Last year, the Food and Drug Administration investigated an undisclosed number of cases in which Chinese-made pesticides had been found in the fruit and vegetables sold in grocery stores.

According to Bachmann, the Chinese government is aware of the problems and will attempt to tackle them during the spring and summer in a bid to attract more foreign investment.

The European Union had planned to ban China's exports of pesticides to Europe in January 2013, amid growing concerns over their alleged use in the manufacture of deadly insecticides. China has responded with a plan to stop imports of honey and seafood from the EU, as well as food and wine, for six months, but it has now extended imports of those products by another six months.

The European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) has also been embroiled in controversy over the use of chlorpyrifos, the chemical that has been banned in the United States for more than 20 years. It was responsible for finding the first trace of the pesticide in the 1980s. The European commission is now reviewing whether to continue using it.

The European trade body Europol issued a press release this week urging that the use of the pesticide should be curtailed to "prevent any further health risks to consumers". A spokesman, Mark Adams, said: "We strongly support the removal of chlorpyrifos from the EU pending further research."

The European Union's environment commissioner, Janez Potocnik, has been a vocal opponent of chlorpyrifos, arguing in May that it was not yet proven that there were no health risks associated with it. In May, she said it was too late for the pesticides to be banned: "The risks [of chlorpyrifos] had already been assessed, and we were aware that the EU Commission would have to act." Last month, the European Environmental Bureau asked for an extension to the ban until 2017, pending further studies. Potocnik has also asked EFSA head Sir Richard Carr to investigate the use of pesticides after it emerged that he had met the head of a Chinese agency who had asked him to investigate whether it was safe to use them in China.

The trend of people living with the condition in Ontario is growing at a faster pace than in most other provinces, with a disproportionate impact on young individuals and children.

Statistics Canada reveals that the number of individuals living with multiple sclerosis in Ontario has doubled over the past decade. The data also highlight the vulnerability of young people to the condition.

"A condition whose symptoms can become so complex that people may need to amputate a limb can have a profound and unpredictable impact on all aspects of people's lives," said Dr. Sarah Burt, medical director at St. Joseph's Hospital in Toronto. "Unfortunately, the best we can do for our patients is to keep them as active as possible, and provide them with as normal a life as possible."

Individuals living with multiple sclerosis (MS) are those whose nervous system is inflamed due to a malfunction or lack of a specific immune system component. The illness is chronic and occurs when myelin, a thin fatty tissue coating on nerve fibers, is lost. This results in damage to the brain or nervous system, loss of mobility, and eventually loss of function in the fingers, toes, muscles, or arms.

The disease was first identified in the mid-19th century and had a relatively low prevalence in Canada over the past 100 years. Only a few people with MS lived close to their families, especially those born after 1900.

Researchers have linked the disease to environmental toxins, but also found that it can be triggered by environmental factors. When the body cannot control myelin, nerve cells die rapidly, and the cells connecting sensory nerves to muscles are damaged. MS is often triggered by exposure to specific chemicals, including benzopyrene, a constituent of cigarette smoke. Although researchers cannot identify the exact chemicals or chemicals that trigger the disease, they know that exposure to these chemicals results in immune function abnormalities and inflammation.

According to Dr. Burt, there have been several developments in medical treatments that may have helped decrease the incidence of the disease, such as the use of topical steroids. However, there are also steps the public can take to ensure their children and young adults are healthy.

"The best thing for any child or young adult is to keep them active and encourage them to participate in physical activities when they are ready," she said. "Some medications that may help are those that affect the immune system without interfering with normal functioning. However, if you have chemical exposure, such as exposure from cigarette smoke, that is likely one of the things we should focus on."

To address the rising trend of the condition, Dr. Burt stated that the next medical research initiative will be to figure out how to reduce the toxicity of various substances. "We already know that medications have an effect on the immune system; we need to work to identify the chemicals that are affecting us."

The rising rates of multiple sclerosis have garnered attention from health officials across the province. In March, a new strategy for the public was released, creating a central office of MS. This office reports to Dr. Burt and will coordinate the various divisions and agencies tasked with monitoring and combating multiple sclerosis.

In the 2015/16 fiscal year, one person with multiple sclerosis was diagnosed per every 28,738 people in the province, and one young person died of MS every 27. The disease affects more males than females in Ontario, with 7.6 deaths per 100,000 among males. However, female MS cases tend to be underreported.

MS can cause a range of physical problems, including impaired vision, loss of balance, and joint pains. The condition can also lead to dementia, heart problems, and high blood pressure.

For more information on MS, visit St. Joseph's Health Centre's MS and Multiple Sclerosis website.
