I recently gave a talk on the current state of the indie dev scene at GDC 2013 in San Francisco. While at GDC, I noticed a lot of questions about the status and future of indie game development. Some people said things like, "Why invest time and money into indie games? They're too difficult to make!"

I wrote a simple blog to explain why indie games are easier to make and better received in the wider market. After reading the blog, I was surprised to see many people share their opinions without reading the blog itself.

So, I decided to re-publish this blog at GDC as an easy-to-read post and in case you don't have time to read it in detail, here's a summary:

Indiegogo doesn't care about your funding goal. It depends on your game. If your game will sell for $30-$100+ on Steam, that's okay. Otherwise, a little less. If you use a F2P model with a game that earns money, you'll attract more buyers.

For that reason, it's better to use an F2P model with a game that earns a little money. For example, a free-to-play model. Indiegogo won't allow developers to sell more than what they've already raised. This will be useful for people who didn't receive any backers.

The only way the community will change is if they get to have their voices heard. And it's always better if people who don't have an idea and/or money to do the pitch, share their ideas before others do.

But how can you get your ideas heard? What do you have to do? Here's a quick and simple guide:

1) Get people involved in your game

The most important thing to do is get people involved! A successful campaign will have your backers and your developers as supporters who care about your project.

2) Share what you have

A successful campaign won't be judged by how many people know about it... but how awesome your game is! Keep the game under wraps!

If you plan to get a lot of reviews, don't forget to check this page: http://indiedb.com/games-for-review/

3) Post a link on Twitter and Facebook

Indie game developers have a hard time creating something unique and different. The reason is, people can't tell what you're doing unless they play it and then they know that a specific indie game has been done before.

In other words, make sure you share your game on Twitter and social media and have a Facebook page.

4) Find out what you need from Kickstarter

The most important thing I learned for my kickstarter campaign is that I needed a few things from Kickstarter as well that other developers should know.

I needed to have a detailed pitch for everyone to know what I have, where the money is being spent and how the game will generate revenue. What it will cost you and, what are the rewards that will be delivered with the money pledged.

I needed to get access for a designer to do a playable prototype in order to show everybody what I have planned and get an estimate of how long it will take us.

You need to know how do you deliver it. Where are you going to go? Where is the money coming from? I had to know these things and be able to show others on what I should be planning. At the same time it was important that I not put the money into something that I cannot keep working on at the time. That means, you must plan to be financially independent for a number of years. And, that means that your money might not be there anymore!

Also, if you have a great game, but are struggling to get the money, you should not get into the idea of pitching for a kickstarter! Kickstarter is not for that.

You should instead plan to find a small enough amount of money that you are confident you can finish the game by yourself and get it out for the community to know about and then do crowdfunding.

5) Be creative!

A successful kickstarter campaign gives you the opportunity to get media attention to your project.

A brief pause in the ongoing campaign season allowed former President Barack Obama to take a moment to reflect on his own legacy.

The former President remarked that "it's fair to say that if our political system had been designed around the premise that the average American is well-served by having a single political party, we might well not be in the situation we're in" following the November election.

However, our system wasn't designed for that. It was designed around coalitions. And today, more than ever, we need coalitions," Obama said.

It is true that in the United States, both major political parties have "coalitions of interest." Some of those coalitions — like the one backing Democratic candidate Hillary Clinton — are clearly in favor of the current administration. There was also the coalition that supported Barack Obama's reelection in 2012 (and the one that backed Clinton) and the one backed by the Republican Party and its billionaire donors backing President Trump (but that latter coalition hasn't shown much support for Trump thus far).

That's not to say that this isn't a complicated political system. But coalitions aren't the central problem. It's all about one simple idea: The American political system is intended to be based around a party system.

The system was created in the 1830s to break up political blocs of the Whig Party — a conservative political party led at the time by Andrew Jackson and John Quincy Adams — and the Democratic Party — a liberal party led by Andrew Jackson and Abraham Lincoln.

The plan worked remarkably well for over a century. With all the parties divided, the country was protected from the evils of both parties — the corruption of the political class for big business, the isolationism of the anti-slavery parties, the fear of political parties from the far Left and Right, and so on.

With those coalitions set in stone, the American system worked exactly how the President intended it to work. Presidents appointed senators and governors, who appointed members of Congress. When each party controlled enough power in Washington, it was easy to get major legislation passed.

This continued under presidents like Rutherford B. Hayes, Chester A. Arthur, William McKinley, Teddy Roosevelt, Calvin Coolidge, and, of course, Franklin D. Roosevelt — a great President, by all accounts, though not the most popular when his two terms were over. Even his successor Herbert Hoover, though elected to his eighth term, was viewed as an out-of-touch, self-centered liberal. For a long time after he retired from the White House, the Democrats in Congress were seen as obstructionist, and the Republicans in Congress were seen as obstructionist, too. Congress was always in the control of one party.

That's not to say that Republicans got all that much worse than the Democrats during the administrations of those who followed Hoover. The big parties weren't exactly in agreement on major issues. President Dwight Eisenhower disagreed with Dwight D. Eisenhower, and vice president Richard Nixon and Gerald Ford were not exactly allies, either. This, however, was not unusual.

In recent years when the parties have become more divided, as they have over the last 10 years, Americans have been less united. During this time, the country's political system has been less in control. Both parties have less influence. The country's leaders are no longer in lockstep and are unable to get anything done. The country's politicians are often more interested in appeasing their more extreme sides than in serving the interests of the vast majority of the country.

And yet, despite all these problems, the American political system persists.

The most surprising thing about our system is how often it works. As Obama said, no one "should have any illusion that the system is working pretty well."

Partisan dysfunction

Over the past year, two partisan groups — Senate Republicans (who were unified in their opposition to Obama's agenda) and House Republicans (who were unified in opposition to Trump's agenda) — have made two very different approaches to Washington, D.C.

For the entire decade of the George W. Bush administration, House Republican lawmakers and Senate Republicans voted together 98.5 percent of the time. For the first 13 years of the Obama administration, House Republicans and Senate Republicans voted together 98.4 percent of the time. The concept of revaluation is a crucial aspect of currency management, particularly when the value of a currency changes and the government seeks to adjust its valuation in accordance with shifting real exchange rates.

What is a foreign exchange?

Foreign exchange refers to the conversion of a private currency to a public market, thereby allowing for the exchange of currency without a circulating value. This concept is often used in private banking systems, where individuals can exchange their currency for another at a designated rate.

What is revaluation?

Revaluation is the process by which an issuer adjusts the value of a currency based on changes in real exchange rates. This can be achieved through a variety of methods, including the "change to" process, where the issuer buys foreign exchange at a more advantageous price.

The issuer can also use the proceeds from the sale of a particular bond to issue foreign currency, which can then be used to purchase foreign bonds or U.S. bonds. This allows the issuer to revalue the currency without affecting its premarket value.

The celestial body known as Mars holds a fascinating secret. Its core contains a substantial amount of mass, which, if extrapolated, would result in a ring approximately 200 to 300 kilometers in diameter. This ring would have the capacity to encase all the liquid water that has ever existed on the planet.

The concept of this ring offers potential insights into the possibility of life on Mars.

"I have long been intrigued by the prospect of liquid water on Mars," said the lead author of a recent study, Peter Smith of the University of Colorado, US.

"What if there existed a thick, impermeable layer of ice in an ice-altered region, safeguarding the liquid in the core from exposure to the atmosphere?"

The answer lies in the discovery of an ice ring, as reported this week in a scientific journal.

The ice layers at the top and bottom of the ring are sufficiently thin to remain undetected by telescopic observation.

However, if they were composed of a more substantial material, they would be visible to telescopes utilizing a process called gravitational microlensing.

This phenomenon is triggered by a slight alteration in the movement of stars within an observer's field of view.

One method employed by the researchers is called gravitational microlensing.

If Earth were being affected by the gravitational pull of a massive celestial body such as Mars, it would be subject to this effect.

In the case of Mars, the effect would only be observable for a portion of the planet, as depicted in the accompanying image.

Earth is not being affected, and thus remains exposed throughout the planet.

"We discovered several possible locations where the thickness of the ice layer corresponds to similar distances from the Sun as Earth's orbital distance from the Moon," said Smith.

"This distance indicates that the thickness of the ice ring is more than a few hundred kilometers – just shy of a kilometer."

The ring is found to be more than 5,000 kilometers deep and more than 2,000 kilometers wide – equivalent to two Earth diameters in size.

At least 40 per cent of the planet is covered in large ice rings, or large ice spheres. This could have protected Martian soil from water and allowed habitable conditions to occur long enough for life to evolve.

If true, Mars' hollow nature would render this ring unique in its size and age. So far, only three planets orbiting stars other than the Sun have been observed to possess rings.

The moon, on the other hand, is thought to be composed of solid rock.

I've always had a passion for cooking. When I'm not busy, I like to experiment with new recipes and techniques. I've recently discovered a love for cooking for others, whether it's for family gatherings or just a quiet night in. I've also been exploring the world of Pinterest and have found a great community of like-minded individuals who share my enthusiasm for cooking.

One of my favorite recipes to date is this one. It's a classic, and for good reason. It's been a staple in my household for years, and I've even had the pleasure of sharing it with loved ones. You can find similar recipes online, but I think this one stands out for its unique flavor and texture.

This recipe is a go-to for me when I'm cooking pasta. It's easy to make and requires just a few simple ingredients. The key is to take your time and let the flavors meld together. A little bit of fresh parsley and basil can make all the difference in the world. And of course, the star of the show is the sauce itself. It's worth the extra effort to make your own, trust me.

Here's the recipe:

Tomato Basil Lasagna with Feta Pasta

Ingredients:

* 2 cups whole peeled tomatoes or diced tomatoes
* 3 tbsp fresh parsley (chopped)
* 1/2 cup olive oil
* 2 tbsp chopped basil
* 2 garlic cloves
* 1 can whole peeled tomatoes or diced tomatoes
* 1 lb fettuccine
* Handful fresh parsley
* 1/2 tsp salt
* Paprika (optional)
* Extra virgin olive oil (as needed)

Method:

1. Peel tomatoes and chop. Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add tomatoes and sauté until completely softened, about 5 minutes.

2. Return tomatoes to the pot and add in parsley, basil and garlic. Continue to sauté until fragrant and caramelized. About 1-2 minutes. If needed, add in salt and/or paprika. Let simmer for 10 minutes.

3. Add in fettuccine (or a large pasta) and tomatoes. Cover and let cook for about 20 more minutes until fettuccine has fully absorbed all of the sauce. Taste and season with salt, paprika and extra virgin olive oil. If necessary add more garlic and additional basil. Serves 6.

The art of transforming a numerical sequence from its binary form to its decimal equivalent is a relatively straightforward process. Here's a step-by-step guide to achieve this:

First, take note of the binary sequence. Next, assign a value to each digit starting from the rightmost position. The values increase by one for each successive digit, beginning with 0. 

Subsequently, multiply each digit's value by the corresponding power of 2. The rightmost digit's value should be multiplied by 2 to the power of 0, the second rightmost digit's value should be multiplied by 2 to the power of 1, and so on.

Finally, add up all the products obtained in the previous step to arrive at the decimal equivalent of the binary number. 

Let's illustrate this process with the binary number 1011, which is equivalent to 11 in decimal.

Begin by writing down the binary number: 1011. 

Assign values to each digit: 1 * 2^3 + 0 * 2^2 + 1 * 2^1 + 1 * 2^0. 

Calculate the products: 8 + 0 + 2 + 1 = 11.

Add up the products: 11.

Therefore, the decimal equivalent of 1011 is indeed 11. I hope this clarifies the process for you. If you have any further questions, please don't hesitate to ask.

The following peregrine falcons, recently captured in North Carolina, were not, in fact, part of the federally protected species.

"It's a bit of a letdown," said Jason Kremers, the director of the Peregrine Fund's North Carolina team. "We had hoped for a different outcome."

The announcement from the agency comes shortly after the North Carolina Wildlife Resources Commission voted to euthanize three peregrines due to a lack of evidence that they were part of the federally protected population.

"This is disheartening for us not only because of the current situation, but also because it means we won't be able to save one of their kind," Kremers said.

It wasn't until December that the Fish and Wildlife Service decided the four birds, known as the Macon 4 peregrines, shouldn't be protected, despite receiving permits from the federal agency to release them.

While the agency didn't provide an explanation for the decision, officials with the federal agency stated that the peregrine species "can't reliably be identified on the face of the permit record without a visual examination," officials said in a statement.

As the news was announced, there was no mention of the Macon or the other birds under the federal agency's protection. North Carolina Wildlife Resource Commission officials were unavailable for comment on Monday.

In 2013, officials with the Fish and Wildlife Service confirmed that an endangered species, the bald eagle, was not protected under the Endangered Species Act, The Associated Press reported.

As a result, the agency released bald eagles from a federal reserve in California that had been closed since 2004 under the Act.

The Macon 4 were captured last month near Charlotte by David Moulton, director of the Center for Predator-Free North Carolina, who was in the process of putting a tracking tag on the birds. Moulton called the peregrines' release a mistake.

Since December, there has been no word from the federal agency.

If the four birds are not officially protected now, the Fish and Wildlife Service is supposed to provide a ruling in the next 90 days, Kremers said. The agency said it has scheduled a meeting for January 14 to look at options for protecting the birds.

While the falcons remain in captivity, the North Carolina Wildlife Resources Commission said a hearing on their fate was scheduled for next Tuesday in Wake County Superior Court before Magistrate Justice Frank E. Smith.

The Peregrine Fund and other federal organizations called on the Fish and Wildlife Service to re-examine its decision.

The mineral fluoride is a natural element that occurs in seawater and other bodies of water. It is added to public water supplies to prevent tooth decay. Fluoride is also a key contributor to tooth decay in children. When ingested, fluoride binds to tooth enamel and interferes with the body's ability to absorb fluoride naturally.

Many people are exposed to fluoride through water fluoridation, food additives, medicine, and medications. In your home, fluoride absorption from fluoride in drinking water is largely through ingestion and through tooth decay. Food and beverage products, such as tea, cocoa, sugar, and coffee, can also contain fluoride. Medicines, such as sodium thiopental and fluorouracil, contain fluoride.

To reduce fluoride exposure in your home, you can eliminate sources of fluoride, especially from tap water. You can also use non-medication dental products, such as fluoride mouth rinses and toothpowders. Avoid food and beverages that contain high amounts of fluoride, such as tea, pizza dough, and bread. Additionally, avoid tobacco products and alcohol, which contain fluorides.

When you brush your teeth with toothpaste that contains fluoride, the fluoride material is absorbed through the enamel during tooth brushing. It enters the bloodstream and is used by cells as a food source. When you swallow fluoride, fluoride ions enter the body and are used as a dietary or drug source.

The amount of fluoride in fluoridated water varies by region, and the amount of fluoride in your teeth is determined by the age of your teeth and the amount of time you have consumed fluoridated water.

The concept of "message discipline" is often used in political communications, and as a political consultant, I find it to be a valuable tool. It has become a bit of a cliché, but it's still an important concept to understand.

When working with a group, message discipline is crucial for managing messaging and decision-making. This is especially important for larger groups that need to interact with voters regularly. The messaging and decision-making process must evolve constantly, and message discipline is a key tool for keeping things under control.

In this post, I'll provide an overview of how message discipline works within organizations and discuss some tactics for maintaining it. Next week, I'll explore the tools organizations use to maximize the effectiveness of their messaging.

Why Is Message Discipline Important?

Organizations have various reasons for implementing message discipline, including cost savings, recruiting better candidates, and engaging voters. However, it's particularly useful for organizations with large numbers of members. By having a single, focused message, an organization can stay on top of what people are talking about and use that information to make better decisions about communication.

Let me provide an example. Suppose you're a local community organization tasked with developing and promoting local candidates. The top candidates come from various communities, and you're the authority on those candidates. When people ask questions about the candidates, you might focus on their strengths and the message they're trying to convey, rather than getting bogged down in details.

How Do You Achieve Message Discipline?

To get your message discipline right, it's essential to focus on what's truly important. This means concentrating on what people care about and what they want, rather than getting caught up in minor details. It's also important to be consistent, clear, and purposeful in your messaging.

Here are five key principles to keep in mind when implementing message discipline:

1. Focus on what you're trying to communicate and with whom you're communicating.
2. Concentrate only on what's important.
3. Make sense of complex information and present it in a clear and concise manner.
4. Be consistent in your messaging across all channels.
5. Stay true to your purpose and values.

By following these principles, you can develop an effective message discipline strategy that helps you achieve your goals.

I began working on a software project, but the original author never gave me permission to share it. He made a comment that if I had paid him, I could trust him. I didn't want to trust him, but I also didn't want to share it anyway. Then he disappeared.

I recently finished reading a book and it reminded me of this experience. I'm grateful for the support and encouragement I've received from my friends and peers.

I wanted to share some lessons I learned while working on my first open source project.

First, I learned that trust can be lost quickly. People who don't support or help you can be friends or former colleagues. I've been fortunate to have friends who supported me, but they can become enemies.

Second, I learned the importance of taking responsibility for my decisions. If I wanted to do it right, I could follow best practices and comply with licenses. However, the more I learned, the more complicated it became. There are many different licenses and ways to do things, and I still struggle to ensure compliance.

I've had experiences where I couldn't make decisions, and friends would tell me what to do. Sometimes, I just couldn't decide, and that's okay.

I also learned to recognize my own mistakes and make my own decisions. I'm glad I didn't push forward with a project that wasn't right for me.

Once you have a community behind you, things get interesting. You'll work with people who are honest and make you feel like you're part of something special. I couldn't have reached my current level without the support of my friends and peers.

The third thing I learned is the importance of having a process for voicing concerns. Technology is key to ensuring success. A developer's success depends on more than just their code, but also the tools they use and how they interact with others.

Contribution can't always be measured by new features or documentation. Sometimes, people's input is crucial, and we need to consider it.

One of the biggest challenges is ensuring the team doesn't work against the community that created the project. I'm fortunate to work for a company that doesn't do community development, but in most cases, the original developer doesn't hand the project over to a community group or individual.

I was asked why I didn't write an open source library. The answer was simple: I didn't want to be the last to know about changes. I wanted to give people who depend on my library the ability to see code changes easily.

There are two major problems with this statement. First, if your project depends on others, they'll get the changes. You'll have to open your code to everyone.

The methodology behind the ranking: We examined TV by the Numbers' data on digital streams and counted downloads of all episodes from the top five digital properties (CW Seed, DC Universe Online, The CW's website, The CW's app, The CW app for iOS and Android, and the CW app for Apple TV & Roku — more information on each is available on the respective properties). This also encompasses digital streams on streaming video platforms — acquiring a show to stream on Hulu or similar platforms, for instance, can be quite challenging.

To gauge digital viewership, TBS and Adult Swim were also included: The CW has never ranked in the top five on the respective networks, yet that does not mean it lacks a strong digital footprint. On CW Seed, you can search by series (or search for "CW" or "CW Seed"), series title, or author, and there you'll find series' trailers, photos, a full description of the show, cast, and more. Both apps can be free (both on Apple TV and on Roku) and will display episode titles, full descriptions, trailers, video clips, and more, but if you wish to watch some of the CW Seed catalog on your mobile device, they cost $7-$15 per episode.

He began his academic pursuits at the University of Munich, where he earned scholarships from both the Catholic-affiliated University of Munich and the Lutheran-affiliated Universitas in Münster.

Hilbert's most famous contribution to mathematics is his work on the foundations of mathematics, which he presented in a series of lectures at a mathematical conference in 1921. In these lectures, he explored the idea that mathematics is not just a collection of abstract concepts, but rather a language that can be used to describe the world around us.

One of the key insights Hilbert gained from his work was the importance of mathematical patterns and symmetries. He believed that these patterns and symmetries were not just aesthetic features of mathematics, but rather a reflection of the underlying structure of the universe. To explore this idea, Hilbert developed a new approach to mathematics, which he called the "pure mathematics approach."

This approach involved using mathematical proofs to establish the existence of patterns and symmetries in mathematics. Hilbert's goal was to show that these patterns and symmetries were not just accidental, but rather a fundamental feature of the mathematical universe.

One of Hilbert's most famous theorems, known as Theorem I, is a prime example of this approach. In this theorem, Hilbert proves that the set of all possible sets of size n is a subset of the set of all possible infinite sets. This theorem has far-reaching implications for our understanding of mathematics and the nature of reality.

In conclusion, David Hilbert's work has had a profound impact on the development of mathematics, and his ideas continue to influence mathematicians and physicists to this day. His legacy is a testament to the power of human curiosity and the importance of exploring the mysteries of the universe.

The tech giant ultimately put its plans on hold in February 2015 and agreed to sell itself to Verizon for a cash consideration of $4.8 billion and a majority stake in Alibaba in August. The CEO of Yahoo, Marissa Mayer, has expressed high expectations for the company's new mobile video advertising platform, which recently became available.

"This is a significant milestone for us," said Mayer. "The closure of the acquisition is a testament to the dedication of our team," added the Chief Financial Officer of Yahoo, Ken Goldman. "Together, we will continue to focus on driving growth and strengthening our core businesses, while investing in our growth opportunities."

The acquisition also marks Yahoo's transition from a dominant desktop platform to a more mobile-centric approach, as smartphones and tablets have become the primary sources of media consumption for consumers. "I'll be the first to acknowledge that this was a significant step backward," said Goldman. "We should have issued a warning sign two years ago."

"No matter where you look, there are more choices for consumers today," said Goldman. "They're coming in a variety of sizes and brands."

The acquisition marked the final major change for Yahoo's core business, which had been in turmoil since the surprise resignation of CEO and co-founder Jerry Yang on September 15, 2012, followed by the departure six days later of Chief Financial Officer Ken Goldman. A search for his replacement quickly found a new CFO in Kenneth Goldman, who took over.

Goldman described Yahoo on stage on the opening day of the company's initial public offering: "This was the last chance for Yahoo!" However, Yahoo's struggles were far from over.

As of November 15, 2015, Yahoo recorded a net loss of $4.4 billion on revenues totalling $3.15 billion. The company was forced to suspend some payment operations and sell off several of its non-core assets after its CEO quit and Yahoo had to restructure its operations.

And on November 15, one year after Yahoo announced plans to sell itself, the deal was finally closed. The acquisition, which included Yahoo's advertising business, Yahoo Japan, and the remaining stake in Alibaba, valued Yahoo at $4.8 billion, about $2.8 billion more than the company paid for itself in cash and stock two years ago. The two companies have worked together to launch a new advertising platform called Tumblr, which they hope will eventually be able to monetize more users online.

February 2017 saw the release of President Trump's budget, a comprehensive plan to reshape the federal government. One of his campaign promises was to eliminate the $19,000 annual grant funding for the Corporation for Public Broadcasting, the public media arm of the Federal Communication Commission. The president's cuts aim to boost funding for local stations and grant the FCC the power to restrict the Corporation for Public Broadcasting's funding to public broadcasting stations in more than four-fifths of the country.

This isn't the first time the Corporation for Public Broadcasting has been in Trump's crosshairs. During his presidential campaign, Trump vowed to end "crony capitalism" in Washington when it came to tax breaks and subsidies. However, the budget is just one part of a broader attack on public broadcasting, which the president has dubbed "public enemy No. 1." Last January, NPR's vice president of communications explained why this label was so inappropriate.

"The thing is, it's not a single entity. It's an idea," says Vivian Schiller. "The idea of public TV and radio and radio stations and a public media presence are ideas. The Corporation for Public Broadcasting, as we call it here, is an entity, and that thing's been around for almost thirty years and for many of the same reasons the idea was started."

This is one of the main reasons Trump is likely to be disappointed in the Republican budget he plans to unveil in the coming months. The budget proposed to slash federal funding for public broadcasting by over 20 percent and would allow the Corporation for Public Broadcasting to die while also ending tax credits that Congress gave to the Corporation for Public Broadcasting so that it wouldn't have to pay back taxes on some of the proceeds it receives.

"The idea that there would be some giant group of bureaucrats that would come to your community, and give you a grant, and make it their mission to get public broadcasting on the air, that is a really important piece of the American idea," says Schiller. "That's part of why America exists, but it's also one of the pillars of a good democracy."

The President's budget also calls for reducing funding for the Corporation for Public Broadcasting by 10 percent. "I think that that's completely misguided and very counterproductive," says Schiller, who joined NPR in May.

Schiller says a key reason for the Republican budget's cuts is that the Republican-controlled House wants to move away from the Corporation for Public Broadcasting's subsidy formula, which is what ensures that the agency remains able to reach low-income and lower-population areas. "They're basically taking money out of the Corporation for Public Broadcasting and putting it into these programs that can only spend money on people who live in a certain income range and in an income division that can only be funded by tax credits. But it's not the case with all of their tax credits," says Schiller.

On the ninth of February, 2016, a significant milestone will be celebrated by the university and the community. It marks the 150th anniversary of the establishment of a student and athletic organization known as Sigma Phi Epsilon (SxE) at the University of Michigan (UM).

The story of SxE began in 1888 when Samuel Gompers, the president of the University's College of Engineering, received a request from the University's women's athletics director to establish an athletic club that would rival the men's teams. At the time, the University only offered a few sports, and a rival team was considered a hindrance to women's basketball players.

Gompers decided upon the name SxE to honor the engineering schools and the engineer that started it all, William M. Robinson. A former engineering student in his 30s, Robinson made strides to improve the physical safety of women, including an invention for a "safety glove" that gave women better control over their hands.

Despite its initial success, Robinson died in 1905 from a heart attack that ultimately claimed his life several months after the founding of SxE. The club disbanded on May 15, 1888, with only 25 members, which is what is displayed on the university buildings, until the early years of the 1900s when it began to grow to 1,500 women in a handful of clubs.

The founding members of SxE did not include all female members of the women's basketball team, but rather a smaller group of athletic women who joined the organization in order to continue to play their field hockey, softball, and volleyball. These women would also go on to become significant members of the school's athletic programs and later serve within and beyond their alma mater.

Throughout the 1970s and 1980s, the number of women in the university's university athletic teams grew to approximately 20,000. In 1983, a new women's swim team was added to Michigan's team, and it became the only women's program in Michigan that qualified for NCAA tournaments for a decade.

The growth of the women's teams continued to increase through the 1990s and 2000s, at which point the number of members in the university athletic teams became larger, growing to over 55,000 by 2011.

SxE was not only a place where women could play an athletic sport – it was also a haven for women," said Susan Brown-Simmons who is one of the few members of the university's athletic teams outside of SxE. "I could play volleyball on Saturdays at SxE without my family and people from my sports teams feeling awkward."

Despite this growth, the University did not officially recognize SxE until 2001.

When it officially joined the university, members of the organization had the chance to choose how they wanted to be represented. In 2002, members of SxE chose to be represented by their original name of "Sigma Phi Epsilon." In recognition of the organization's contributions to Michigan's athletic teams, members of SxE chose this name.

Brown-Simmons, who is currently the Associate Director of Women's Athletics Operations for Michigan, spoke with the Detroit Free Press about her experience with the club over the years and its importance to the community.

"When they established SxE, nobody gave it much of a chance," Brown-Simmons said. "There was a lot of skepticism in the community about women's athletics at the time. It has taken a great deal more than skepticism to change the minds and hearts of the football and basketball fans."

SxE continues to play an important role in Michigan's culture in a variety of areas.

Brown-Simmons, who has played volleyball for more than 30 years and is one of the few women to have played for Michigan as a freshman, said that she thinks of the organization and the impact that it has had on her team even when she is not playing on it. "I always see the spirit that we play with," Brown-Simmons said. "They are a really special group, the spirit in that [SxE] room is just amazing."

For more information on the Michigan SxE club, visit the women's basketball page on the Michigan SxE website.

In the summer of 1916, a pivotal moment in the First World War unfolded on the Western front. On July 16th, German forces launched a significant operation, but their efforts were hindered by the poor quality of the trenches and the numerous trenches dug by the French and British after years of trench warfare. A British soldier aptly described trenches as "the worst thing in the world," yet they had not been utilized extensively.

Confronted with two fronts against one enemy, the German army made a series of mistakes that undermined their chances of success:

The German army failed to establish solid defensive positions, instead opting for a makeshift defense and subsequently retreating, leaving behind no trenches or strong positions. This allowed the French and British to dig up their trenches and reopen them in a more continuous fashion, enabling them to expand their defenses and secure more of the battlefield.

The German army failed to concentrate its troops, scattering its forces across the front without intention of returning, thereby allowing the French and British to quickly organize their forces and move towards the German trenches.

The German army failed to prepare its troops adequately, with Commander Albert Kesselring being too cautious and not taking the necessary steps to prepare his troops in advance of the war. Kesselring attempted to utilize British artillery and inferior German equipment, resulting in failure on both fronts.

The German army failed to exploit its numerical superiority, with Kesselring's soldiers outnumbering the British and French by several times in 1915 and by almost four times on the eastern front. By 1916, the Germans relied on their own reserves to fight a war against superior numbers.

The German army failed to take advantage of the limited French and British strength, with the French and British mustering approximately 6,000 men each, less than 1% of the German army's total strength.

The German army struggled to adapt to the unpredictable terrain on the Western front. When attempting to take a narrow ridge overlooking the city of Ypres on July 16, 1916, the Germans were forced to retreat. The Germans had assembled a significant force on one front facing the French and British on the other side of the ridge, but the French and British were able to reorganize their forces and quickly repel the German forces.

The German army was slow to recognize the need for proper trench organization and tactics. For over a month, the French and British constructed an effective trench network with the aid of British artillery. By 1915, trench warfare in Europe had reached a stalemate, and the Germans were unable to effectively exploit their numerical superiority and mass formations to attack the trench systems.

The German army had a poor understanding of the nature of war. After the German army lost both Meuse-Argonne and the Somme, it found itself fighting a war that was much deeper than initially thought:

The Western front was the largest and most complex of any at the outset of the First World War. Its fighting fronts spanned over 2 million square miles, stretching from the North to the Baltic, and from the North Sea to the Baltic. Its theaters of combat crossed nine foreign nations and five continents, spanning an area extending from the Black Sea to the Himalayas. At its core, the Western front was a struggle to establish a "Greater Europe." Allying with England in September 1914, Germany hoped to dominate Central and Eastern Europe as an extension of the German Empire. France, Italy, Belgium, and Russia challenged the German claim, believing that a Greater Empire would lead to Germany being the dominant power across the East. At the same time, the nations of the Western Front recognized the need for a military balance of power to keep the conflict from becoming a one-sided contest. The fighting on the Western front stretched from October 1914 to April 1917, as the Germans fought an uphill battle against both the advancing Allied invasion and the French forces fighting alongside the allies.

A peculiar phenomenon has been observed in the Atlantic bluefin tuna caught off the coast of Australia, with scientists detecting signs of parasites in approximately 10% of the specimens.

By Aurora Nightshade

The prized bluefin tuna, renowned for its exceptional quality and value, continues to face an unprecedented crisis.

Trucks are overflowing with infected and deceased fish, as Australian scientists have identified the presence of parasites in more than 10% of the bluefin caught off Australia in recent years.

These parasites, which cause liver inflammation, are known as hookworms due to their unique attachment to hooks. Researchers have linked the parasite spread to fishing methods that involve using long lines or nets to drag fish in for slaughter.

Satellite trackers placed along the Australian coast have tracked the spread of the parasites, which are not naturally present in bluefin tuna.

The research, conducted by the University of New South Wales and the National Sea University in France, reveals that the parasite is present throughout the Pacific and is being spread along the southern coasts of Australia, New Guinea, and Fiji.

The research highlights the importance of improving fishing methods and serves as a warning to countries that are not efficient in controlling illegal fishing and big-game fishing in their waters.

The European Union has banned catches of bluefin from the Mediterranean and other areas, fearing a massive health crisis.

New Zealand, a frequent bluefin tuna fishing port in the southern Indian Ocean, is not at risk of catching the worms.

More than 60% of the bluefin tuna caught off NSW, Western Australia, Queensland, and Victoria were infected with the parasites.

While some Australian bluefin tuna can be caught using longer traditional techniques, including trawling for sardines, there are concerns that they could also be affected.

Professor Peter Gordon from the University of New South Wales, Australia's leading bluefin shark researcher, is monitoring the distribution of hookworms to determine the extent of the phenomenon.

Mr. Gordon and colleagues are planning to expand the research to Pacific bluefin tuna, which is currently fished commercially in Australia.

In our recent efforts to enhance the upcoming 0.13 Alpha release, we've encountered some unexpected twists. Notably, we've opted to utilize a novel file format, alongside the introduction of auto-save functionality for your saved data. A brief aside, but worth mentioning.

For those unfamiliar with the new file format, I'll provide a concise overview. According to the official release notes:

Fgd files are standalone game files, capable of being compiled for multiple games and platforms.

During the compilation process, they undergo compression, typically in a gzip-compatible format.

These compressed binaries boast a remarkable balance of compact size and substantial data storage. The name might have raised some eyebrows, as it may evoke associations with encryption tools. While the process shares some similarities, it operates under distinct principles.

To simplify the compression and decompression process, let's break it down into two primary methods:

Firstly, we employ dictionary compression, which involves reducing the size of strings by assigning numerical values. This approach is particularly effective when feasible.

Secondly, we utilize file compression techniques, including Huffman coding and LZ77, to compress the file and facilitate rapid loading into RAM. This compression method is also highly effective, provided there is sufficient data for the decompression stage.

For those new to gaming, a.fgd file typically consists of a.exe file paired with an.ogg or.mp3 audio file. The compression and decompression process occurs so swiftly that the file won't need to be copied during uploading to game servers.

After investing a few hours in debugging, I'm pleased to report that we've successfully integrated this information into the game. As always, we welcome feedback on any bugs or suggestions for improving these features.

As far as my personal experiences go, I've only had my dinner declined at a restaurant. I didn't spot it on the menu, nor did I receive a complimentary bonus, nor did the server express gratitude. The individual sitting nearby thought I was quite peculiar for leaving a small token of appreciation. Nobody seemed to go out of their way to accommodate me during that meal.

Many people probably share this sentiment, but that's a misconception. You deserve a small token of appreciation for doing your job correctly. It's not unlike washing your car, taking out the trash, or waiting in line at a grocery store. If it takes you a moment to put the garbage can in the right spot, that's because you weren't fully focused. If you didn't put the toilet seat cover back on, that's because you didn't notice until you did it twice. The goal is to complete the task efficiently, not to rush through as many tasks as possible.

During each dining experience, I would inspect the menu, look for special deals, and if available, ask the server to recommend something. However, only in certain instances did I expect something more in return for a small token of appreciation. You can't simply ask if something is included in the small token, as the server wouldn't know until the small tokens are collected. So, be friendly to your server and suggest that they recommend something that's available. You'll need to be somewhat discreet, but in the end, your server should be grateful for your assistance and the kitchen should appreciate your willingness to help.

I also took a few photographs of my small tokens. If everything is listed in my "notes" section, if not, the cashier would put everything in the order they saw the check leave the small token writer's hands. I used the photograph as a guide to what they should do and left some suggestions for them to include in their menu if things weren't listed on the receipt.

It all depends on the restaurant. When you dine out, you are the master of your own time and space. If you need to depart, you probably do so because you've been waiting an eternity (or because you're taking too long to enjoy your meal), but if you arrive asking for a few minutes to converse then you're likely in a hurry and that can impact what you receive. I'm not suggesting you make a scene, but if you've been waiting a while and you've got some business to attend to, you might want to depart a few minutes early, if only to eat and not have to wait for the check. At that time, you could ask the server or waitress if they could take a few minutes to check on other tables, maybe make new reservations or clean up after the food is consumed.

It's up to you what you do with that extra 30 seconds. Don't prolong your wait unnecessarily and you won't have any regrets while reviewing what you did right and what you did wrong.

The notion that a cherished individual might present you with the most extravagant gift imaginable is a difficult concept to accept, yet the gift of a novel conveyance system comes with a steep price.

A parent from North Carolina, Chris S., has shared with us a tale of a family holiday excursion to Japan that was marred by his daughter's new conveyance system. The story began when, as a special Christmas gift from his father-in-law, Paul S., he decided to take the conveyance system to Japan.

"We acquired the conveyance system in the US, but we traveled to Japan for a visit and planned to stay at a hotel," Chris explained. "The Japanese are known for their sophistication regarding the items they purchase – they do not expect you to bring everything home in a box. I had an electronic reading device and a tablet, and I thought, 'I need both of these to accomplish this.' That was our first mistake."

However, there were some positive aspects: they were treated well during their stay, and upon their return, Chris enjoyed the conveyance system. But then, things took an unexpected turn. They hosted a dinner party with many guests, and the evening progressed with the consumption of wine and champagne. The wine shop owner brought an enormous box of wine, and Chris was offered half the box, with the promise that the owner would keep the gift a secret. Chris was left feeling stunned and confused.

"I received the best dinner party in the world, with people drinking champagne, and I was unable to do anything except take the conveyance system and drive it across town," Chris said. "I purchased a large suitcase and drove across town in the conveyance system, and then I returned to retrieve an electronic reading device or tablet."

On their subsequent trip to Japan, Chris did not have to leave his daughter behind in the United States, although…

"Last summer, we took the same trip, and we were heading towards a lake on the coast of Japan," Chris continued. "I think she was expecting me to fly up to Japan to pick her up. She was not expecting me to have a conveyance system. I did have to change my plans, as I needed to book a ticket to fly to Japan using my American Express card. However, I still had to fly up to Japan."

To make the most of your holiday in Japan, Chris recommends acquiring a conveyance system and then departing the country as quickly as possible. Just be sure to save all your business class seats for the return flight to the United States.

Conservatives may quickly point out that other countries, such as the United Kingdom and Greece, are grappling with a growing deficit, but there is no evidence to suggest that Canada is one of them.

In fact, the Conservatives' failure to make even the slightest effort to control federal finances could potentially cost Canada billions in future revenues.

The government appears unwilling to confront a fundamental problem – how can we reduce our deficits while maintaining federal finances in a state of reasonable health? Over the past decade and a half, each year the federal deficit has grown. Over eight years, the federal government has incurred a $100-billion deficit.

And yet, the Conservatives seem unwilling to address this issue. Instead, they seem unwilling to make even the slightest effort to tackle this significant problem to save money. After eight years of this, they are even unwilling to acknowledge that Canadians are concerned about this spending problem and are asking for change.

The Harper government has invested over $120-billion in new infrastructure projects, many of which are questionable in quality or unnecessary. While the Conservatives claim that the construction of new projects is necessary, Canadians need no reminder that new infrastructure projects rarely create jobs or result in a net gain in economic activity. Instead, they often result in significant cost overruns and cost more than the initial investment.

At the same time, the government has spent billions maintaining a large fleet of aging warships, jets, trucks, and other equipment. These aging equipment upgrades have become bloated, expensive, and inefficient over time. By keeping our fleet of aging equipment at a state of near obsolescence, the federal government is losing out on billions in annual revenue from these outdated tools.

Canada's debt has increased during this current parliament, and is forecasted to be $439-billion for the next three years. There is no new money being spent to pay down that debt. Instead, it is increasing.

At $400-billion, Canada's federal debt-to-GDP ratio is a high number. At least it remains relatively within historical norms. Rather than cutting taxes and balancing the budget by raising taxes, is there a plan that can deliver on what Canadians are asking for – to have a smaller government, a smaller federal debt, and a smarter approach to tax policy?

Rather than trying to find the problem with more government spending, there is a clear and proven method to keeping federal finances in a reasonable state of health. This method is responsible fiscal management.

Fiscal management means balancing the budget not just every year, but every year while also controlling spending for the long term – both for today and for our children and grandchildren.

The NDP, and Canadians across the country, want to live within their means and be sure that they are not taking on debt they cannot afford.

A few months ago, a person named Francesco Bernoulli created a mathematical formula that has become well-known as the Bernoulli formula. The Bernoulli formula describes the tendency for a liquid to remain stationary in a fixed temperature.

In mathematics, it has been used to model the motion of particles in a gas or liquid in a laboratory setting, and the Bernoulli formula is used in various fields, including medicine, physics, and thermodynamics.

The Bernoulli formula is usually written as:

B = C p A, where B is a constant, C is a universal constant, p is a specific heat, and A is an absolute temperature.

C p A is usually referred to as the energy density of a fluid. The heat capacity or thermal mass of a substance is the amount of work needed to raise the temperature of the substance to a particular value. That work is measured in Joules.

In everyday speech, the unit used to measure a chemical or physical value is the joule, a unit of energy. If we consider the universal constant of potential energy C as a unit of energy, we can say that a Joule is the energy required to raise the potential temperature of a liquid or gas of given substance from one temperature to another.

The energy required to raise the temperature of a substance in a laboratory setting is measured in Joules per Celsius degree Fahrenheit of temperature increase. This is given in terms of energy per unit mass of substance.

The Bernoulli formula is often thought to be used to model the motion of a particle in a fluid or a gas. The particle is assumed to have some fixed momentum and it is shown that when p is changed such that p = 0.5, such that the particle will immediately return to its original state, such that if and only if p increases to 1.5 will the particle return to its original state.

If the Bernoulli formula is applied to such a particle, the particle becomes stationary.

Why is this relevant? Well, suppose we have a set of particles and we set their positions x 0, y 0, z 0 and w 0 to be 0.2, 0.8, 2.4 and 6.8 degrees, respectively. We want to know how the particles will move away from the origin after we apply the Bernoulli formula. In other words, what will be the maximum distance from the origin that a particle will move away from at a speed p?

The answer depends on the values of x, y, z, and w. For example, if p = 0.5, the maximum distance is 1.9 cm. If p = 0.3, the maximum distance is 1.4 cm. If we multiply p by 1.6, the maximum distance is 2.8 cm.

We want to use the formula in the laboratory setting for the same set of particles and we know the maximum distance to be 2.8 cm, which is close to the value of 2.6 cm in the laboratory setting. So how can we conclude that the Bernoulli formula tells us the minimum distance to go to and from a maximum value?

The problem with calculating distance from zero is that by definition it is a continuous function of x, y, z and w, for any values of x, y, z, and w. So if we apply the Bernoulli formula to set a variable k such that p = 0.5, we conclude that the maximum distance is in fact 2.5 cm, where the k is a variable. This is the problem with calculating distance from zero for any constant values of x, y, z, and w: We can arrive at any value of k by a large amount of trial and error. But why? Why can't we just use the constant c? And why do we need to know the value n of k and what is n in general? We need to know this because if we were to know n, we can compute a formula for distance, and the formula for distance is:

d(n) = w(k)t(n-p)z/t(n)

where w is a constant, t is the time, z is the velocity along the path, p is the momentum or energy, t is the time, k is the constant representing the distance, and that constant is represented by the universal constant of potential energy.

Last weekend, my partner and I embarked on a four-day adventure to Scotland. We've visited Scotland previously to celebrate her birthday and have a fondness for the country. Although Scottish football isn't as popular as American football, we still enjoyed the experience.

One of the many landmarks we passed was St. Asaph church, located in Dumfries. St. Asaph, like all Scottish churches, has a unique architecture. Its tall, white, and red stone structure bears resemblance to the Catholic Catacombs of Rome and the Roman Colosseum. St. Asaph has remained largely unchanged since its original construction in the 6th century.

The church is notable for another reason; it's the only church that still recites the Divine Liturgy, or the Lord's Prayer. During services, St. George, the patron saint, prays:

O God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.

I believe in thee and I worship thee.

In thy name I hope to obtain eternal life.

I believe that there is no God but thee, the Lord.

I believe thou shalt grant unto me, by thine inspiration, wisdom and strength,

and by the prayers of thy saints, pardon for my sins,

and obtain mercy for my people, O Jesus Christ my Lord. Amen.

This is due to the Church being founded by St. George and St. Edmund, the last two of the seven archbishops of Scotland. It was their prayers, along with those of Sts. Asaph and Dunstan, that were used in the first Liturgy, the Liturgy of the Word.

The fact that St. Asaph didn't modify the Lord's Prayer is what sets it apart.

The Divine Liturgy is a scriptural text that was originally read aloud with the prayer of the Church before the Church. In the Church, the prayer of Scripture is the "Lord's Prayer" or "Great Praised One", spoken by Christ when he instructed the Apostles. Similarly, a priest recites the Lord's Prayer daily.

As we read the Bible aloud, St. Asaph's congregation sings a different version, in which St. George recites the Lord's Prayer. This is called the "Great Praised One," as it is a new form of prayer and language used by St. Asaph. It's a way of praying that is distinct and more intimate than what St. Asaph is accustomed to.

When we read St. George's prayer, we can discover the language of love, forgiveness, and mercy in our lives and in God. This is why we read aloud, as when we read scripture aloud, we are praying the Great Praised One. We don't have to say it aloud, as when we read it, it is recited again by God as he is speaking. When we pray the Lord's Prayer, we are praying the Great Praised One.

Although St. George and St. Asaph were Catholic saints, St. Asaph is not actually Catholic. Although he may have recited the Lord's Prayer in the chapel of St. Asaph, if you visit the Catholic catacombs, with its marble sarcophagi and thousands of skulls as memorials to the dead, it appears that St. Asaph would never have uttered the prayers we do today.

To be Catholic, one must be baptized into the Church. Baptism is a rite in which the laity is immersed in a stream and then washed with wine. Baptism is not a symbolic offering of the Body of Jesus Christ.

Therefore, I'm not baptizing myself into the Church when I recite the Lord's Prayer. Nor am I believing it. Baptism for Catholic children is something they would receive at an age where they would feel ready for it, which, to me, seems more about belief due to my age.

We read "The Lord's Prayer" because we believe it, with all our hearts, with all our souls, believing that God wants us to come to believe it and to pray it. Our faith in the words of the Lord's Prayer is, to me, a spiritual act. Our faith in the words of the Lord's Prayer is our faith in something greater than ourselves.

The notion that the United States Department of Justice has issued a subpoena to Google regarding its alleged ties to Wikileaks is a topic of much speculation. In this context, it is possible that Google could utilize the documents as a basis for litigation, according to Michael Carvin, a New York-based attorney who has represented clients in media and technology-related cases. However, the company may not be able to leverage the subpoenas to compel the government to provide information regarding "the government's alleged use of the courts to chill free speech or suppress opposition political organizations," Carvin noted.

Google and its legal team could attempt to circumvent this issue by arguing to a judge or jury that the information is protected by confidential business and financial information, Carvin suggested. Furthermore, if Google were to assert that the information was not privileged, it could utilize its own privileged information to support this claim, Carvin added.

In theory, a judge would need to consider whether an attorney-client relationship had transpired, Carvin explained. However, there is currently no federal case law regarding whether legal discovery must include a determination from a client.

Carvin opined that the recent WikiLeaks case may have been particularly troubling due to the fact that the government's actions did not constitute a violation of WikiLeaks' First Amendment rights, despite the company's involvement in the release of confidential government files.

The company did, however, provide a copy of its Transparency Report and issued a brief statement explaining its involvement with Wikileaks.

It is likely that the court will have a distinct approach to the issues raised by the Department of Justice, according to Carvin.

"The Department of Justice does not possess the requisite access to Google," Carvin said. "A court decision involving Google will likely be significantly different, as there will be other parties involved in the process, including the Department of Justice and the FBI."

The Department of Justice subpoenaed a Google lawyer and four company employees in April under the Foreign Secrets Act to identify the company's relationships with media organizations that published the leaked Clinton emails.

The Department is reportedly seeking to identify Google's ties with media organizations, as well as the amount of federal advertising the company has paid. According to documents filed with the court, an FBI agent was informed that a confidential informant had reported that someone in a Google executive's position had "known that the FBI's investigation was going to include a look into the possible unauthorized disclosure of confidential information" by the company. The FBI informant also stated that they believed Google had been "actively aiding the FBI or attempting to obstruct the FBI's investigation."

The Justice Department has seized "millions of dollars" worth of Google's advertising since the original FBI investigation began three years ago, according to Ars Technica's Alexa. The U.S. filed court documents requesting an initial seizure of $250,000 worth of Google ads during its investigation that began in July 2014.

In addition, the U.S. sought records related to the activities of Google's "Internet Research Agency," which was accused of running a botnet against political opponents of Russian government on a major political scale that had the ability to infect hundreds of thousands of computers by sending them malicious software.

The Department of Justice has also requested information regarding Google's efforts in the area of government transparency and political advocacy, according to a filing by the Department on May 29.

At the time of this post, the Department of Justice had not responded to a query regarding Google's possible refusal to comply.

The Department of Justice is conducting an ongoing investigation into allegations against Russian intelligence that hackers stole information from the Democratic National Committee, The New York Times reported last month. A source close to the investigation told the Times about a new revelation from the FBI regarding the DNC breach. The source informed the Times that investigators have not yet produced proof of a link between the hackers and the Russians, but that investigators have uncovered "many connections" between the alleged breaches and the Russians.

The investigation into hackers involved in the DNC hack is being led by the FBI following the announcement that then-FBI director James Comey had referred to the DNC's hacking as an "act of war." The Obama administration has blamed Moscow for the DNC hack.

When muscles are subjected to increasing amounts of strain, they become stronger. This occurs when tiny tears form in the muscle fibers as a result of usage. The body then repairs these tears, resulting in thicker and stronger muscle fibers. This process is known as muscle enhancement.

One method to induce strain is to engage in resistance training, such as weightlifting or other forms of resistance exercises. When lifting weights, muscles must work against the resistance, leading to increased strength. Additionally, using one's own body weight as resistance, through exercises like push-ups or squats, can also be effective.

Another method to enhance muscle strength is through high-intensity interval training (HIIT). This involves brief periods of intense exercise followed by periods of relaxation. HIIT can aid in muscle growth and efficiency by increasing the demand for oxygen and nutrients in muscles, potentially stimulating muscle development.

The shimmering phenomenon is a remarkable ability that grants the player's armor an ethereal glow, allowing for stealthy movements. This extraordinary ability is acquired along with the initial tier of tier 60 gear after completing the tutorial. Unlike most other abilities, this one cannot be obtained through tokens of mastery from the PvP Shop.

Abilities

Shimmer

Shimmer (PvE) (Tier 6) 30 yd range Instant 30 sec cooldown Shimmer temporarily imbues the player with an Armor Shimmer effect, granting them stealth for 30 seconds. Stealth prevents all physical damage taken and reduces all damage taken by 25% for 4 seconds. Armor Resists Magic Resists Fire Resists Physical Damage

Armor Shimmer

At level 60, the player can obtain a piece of armor (Tier 6) that will have the ability Armor Shimmer. The armor will be automatically equipped at the same time the Shimmer option is chosen. The armor will have a unique color and texture that resembles armor found in the world, and a golden shine. The armor has no stats, and it is not necessary to equip it to use the ability. Unlike most other effects that reduce the enemy's physical damage, Shimmer is only effective on the target of the player's attack. Note that while the ability is granted on an attack to the player's target, the player is not immune to damage from that enemy during the 30-second stealth, and will take the reduced damage.

The Armor Shimmer effect is unique to each Armor piece, and is a visual effect applied when the player selects that piece to equip. They do not stack, so players can choose whichever gear they like best, each time they equip it. Armor armor pieces have a maximum of 100 Shimmer effects.

Armor: Uniques

The armor pieces have a different appearance depending on the type the armor is from, which can be unlocked in the same manner used for the normal Shimmer. This is reflected in their stats, with some armor pieces making use of a special enchantment.

Armor: Legendary Items

Armor: Factions (except Shattrath City & Stormwind City)

Armor: NPCs

These stats are the base values for the pieces and their upgrades. Higher-level pieces typically grant more stats, while lower-level pieces usually grant more armor. Armor pieces of the same type, however, cannot have different bonuses.

Enchantments

Main-hand and off-hand versions of this ability are always class-specific.

Upgrading

Main-hand and off-hand pieces are upgradable using Shimmer shards and armor scraps. Upgrading requires 10 Shimmer shards and 100 armor scrap. Upgrades can be purchased from the PvP Shop for Shimmer shards.

Upgrading tiers requires a total of 4,250 shards and an average of 1.5 armor scrap per tier. As of patch 7.2, 2 new kinds of armor upgrades were added.

Apple is introducing a new iPhone feature, which is actually not a new feature at all. Instead, it's a limitation. Starting Friday, September 17, the new iPhone will only be able to do one thing.

The iPhone 5 will be released on Thursday, September 25, and it's the most dramatic change since the original iPhone. But before we dive into the details, let's talk about what happened to the other iPhones.

All iPhone 5 devices sold from the original start date in 2007 are on AT&T's network, which has 3.4 million retail stores. The iPhone 5 can work on any other network, but it won't work on Wi-Fi without an Internet connection. There's no SIM card inside, so it can't be used on another network.

Apple has been focusing on providing a faster, more feature-rich smartphone experience, said Tim Cook, Apple's executive chairman. Apple used cellular phones with its current iPod touch, which was last released in 2009, said Cook.

Cellular networks can be costly and less reliable than Wi-Fi, so the iPhone 5 represents an opportunity for Apple to focus more on the Internet. It uses a new wireless chip that uses one of the world's first 4G cellular networks.

The iPhone 5 is already available at dozens of retailers, including Wal-Mart, Target, Best Buy, and Best Buy Mobile, among others.

The iPhone 5 will not be on sale in every store - Wal-Mart is not carrying it, as it's not an iPhone. So you probably won't see it until September 17 - about two months after the iPhone 5 launches. It's not the same as buying an iPhone in a store, since most consumers have to be online to buy.

The iPhone 5 will cost the same as the iPhone 4S - $199 for the 16 GB model, or $299 for the 32 GB - it will not have a new camera option, and Apple isn't offering upgrade options.

The most expensive model, the 32 GB Apple iPhone 5c will cost $549 in gold, $599 in silver or rose gold with a Space Gray back, as first reported by 9to5Mac.

What will happen to other iPhone models? The iPhone 5 still sells at AT&T, Sprint, Sprint Lite, Boost Mobile, T-Mobile, Virgin Mobile, Cricket, Telcel, and in some stores, Verizon. The iPhone 4 and 4S still sell at Verizon and AT&T.

Will you be able to use the iPhone 5 for other apps, media, or documents? Yes, because the new chip works only with an iPhone. The iPhone 5 will work both for iMessages, iBooks, and even iCloud, the company's online file storage service. You can also transfer files between iPhone and iPad.

Will the iPhone 5 get any better performance from the new chip? Apple says the new chip is 10 to 100 times faster compared to the iPhone 4S. So the best performance will be seen in 4G LTE network and Internet applications, like sending iMessages.

Will you be able to send video messages? Yes, Apple is adding video support to its iMessage system this year. You can send video to friends by sending an iMessage. However, it depends on the recipient's iPhone camera capabilities, as Apple can't provide image files. The iPhone 4s could not send an iMessage video with the iPhone 4. Apple can't tell if people will use it.

Will this be the last iPhone? Apple CEO Tim Cook has said he expects the iPhone business to double in the next decade, but declined to reveal any numbers.

In the late 1970s, a group of researchers at the National Institutes of Health conducted a study on the long-term effects of atrazine on laboratory rats. They discovered a significant increase in birth defects, particularly congenital malformations, and concluded that atrazine is a suspected carcinogen. A subsequent study compared the effects of atrazine on female rats' reproductive tracts with those of normal females and found an increase in birth defects, along with abnormalities in the reproductive tract, thyroid, and sperm parameters. The study found that the rats exposed to the highest doses of atrazine and the greatest number of animals suffered the most. A study published in the journal Environmental Toxicology and Chemistry in 2011 found a strong correlation between atrazine exposure and amphibian deformities, with high-dose exposure causing deformities and atrazine causing an average of one deformity per 10,000 amphibians. The study also found that atrazine was present in water pumped from wells and human water in concentrations over 1 part per billion.

The EPA took several years to respond to complaints about the toxicity of atrazine. The scientific investigation found atrazine's effects in fish and the environment consistent with those seen in amphibian deformities, including deformities in frogs, salamanders, and toads. Atrazine was found in water pumped from wells and human water in concentrations over 1 part per billion. In the early 1980s, atrazine was found in drinking water in a small number of Wisconsin communities.

In 1991, the EPA announced a moratorium on the use of atrazine in drinking water due to concerns for public health. The EPA conducted research comparing atrazine exposure with that of other common herbicides and concluded that atrazine was not more toxic than either 2,4-D or dicamba. The EPA did not limit the use of atrazine and began a voluntary reduction in its use, which was completed by 2003. After 2003, the EPA conducted research on the effects of atrazine for the Office of Pesticide Programs and the U.S. Geological Survey.

Despite atrazine being registered in at least 13 states and used in 17 for agricultural purposes, it is not registered in California, Texas, or Washington, and the EPA had no action on the state's registration renewal application in 2016. California became the first state to require registration of atrazine with the EPA, passing a law in 2007 that requires a registration for a new herbicide after it has been sold to any distributor. Colorado and other states have passed similar legislation.

Atrazine uses in farm settings have increased dramatically in recent years, with some states reporting very high amounts. In 2015, the EPA estimated that atrazine concentrations were between 0.9 and 6.4 parts per billion in water supplies and soils in the United States. However, studies conducted by several universities have shown lower concentrations, ranging from 0.09 to 0.18 parts per billion.

The EPA estimates that atrazine is a probable human carcinogen. In 1992, the EPA declared atrazine a probable human carcinogen, indicating to the public that they should be concerned if they drank their water.

On the same day that the House of Representatives approved a one-year extension of the Patriot Act, which was used to collect phone records of millions of Americans, it passed another extension of the FISA Amendments Act, which was used to gather information on foreign leaders. The Obama administration claims that FISA Amendments Act (FAA)—along with other national security laws like the Patriot Act—helps make American safer and has successfully defended the laws in court. Yet, on the same day that the House of Representatives passed the FAA, the House voted in favor of a bill that would require the federal government to reveal the benefits of the F-35 Joint Strike Fighter (JSF), a plane that is behind schedule and over budget.

The House approved the FAA bill despite the fact that it contains no provision preventing the intelligence community from gathering information on Americans. The NSA's activities, particularly under the FAA, have been heavily investigated and found to violate the Constitution's First, Fourth, Fifth, and 13th Amendments. Yet in spite of the recent revelations, it seems that Congress simply can't decide that the constitutional amendments and the privacy rights that they protect are worth much more than a trillion dollars in defense spending.

Although the Senate is currently considering competing legislation that would reform the FISA Amendments Act (FAA), including preventing the government from collecting data on US citizens that doesn't relate to foreign terrorists, it seems that the House—controlled by Republicans—is going ahead with legislation that is less than comprehensive when it comes to curbing the executive branch's power, which has only gotten worse since the creation of the FISA Amendments Act in the 1970s.

"The current bill is too weak," said Rep. Thomas Massie (R-KY). "We need stronger checks, stronger accountability, and we have nothing in this bill to give us real reforms."

It should come as little surprise that these measures were rejected after the House Intelligence Committee published a lengthy report on the FISA Amendments Act and its past oversight, which showed that the Intelligence Community was operating in "a state of secrecy on matters of its warrantless surveillance activities, including its use of FISA." The committee also found that the FISA Amendments Act "violates US constitutional standards for due process and the right to privacy" in that it "is both overbroad in scope and lacks the safeguards and judicial oversight that are necessary to ensure it is constitutional." While the committee called for NSA to cease their unconstitutional spying activities, they expressed the urgency of making "critical improvements" to the law to be more constitutional.

Despite this, the House refused to remove these provisions in the bill and passed its version. After the vote, Massie declared the bill a "disaster."

According to Massie, the reason for passing the bill is that "it has very little chance of passing the Senate," while the House version would make the FAA more constitutional. As it turns out, the House has an incentive to pass the same bill over and over again—a move that Massie believes will benefit the defense industry.

"The only reason the House bill made it through in the first place was because we added an amendment that says that if we were ever able, we would have a sunset in the program," said Massie.

This would make it so that the FAA would sunset in September of 2015.

To help the House pass the bill, Massie and the Tea Party Caucus, along with numerous other rightist conservative groups—such as the FreedomWorks and the Heritage Foundation respectively—agreed to work with House leaders to bring forward multiple amendments. This is a tactic that they have used in the past to get their initiatives through the House, including the Patriot Act extension last year and the USA Freedom Act, which would have created a system to rein in the NSA.

But this time with the FAA, Massie said, "They're doing it the wrong way and taking forever.... If you want my support, let's pass the bill first."

After the vote, Rep. Lynn Westmoreland (R-GA) called on the House to "make the most of a good opportunity" and pass the bill.
