In a hearing at the Old Bailey in London, the girl's parents told the court how they had been told their daughter was ill a few weeks earlier.

The girl was on her way to a birthday party with an older friend when the accused man approached her and said, "I have killed your sister, I killed her - now rape her three times."

The girl died in hospital hours later. She had been raped before her death, one of her killers told police.

'Inconsolable'

Both men were arrested six hours after the murder and the court heard how when police found the body they found she had been stabbed seven times, with a "significant" amount of blood found inside the room.

The court heard when the two arrested men gave police their accounts they denied any involvement in the case and suggested it was possibly a case of a game gone wrong.

But it turned out neither of the men had been involved in her death, the court heard.

The girl - who had been a pupil in the same class as the killers at the same school - reportedly told police she had asked her older friend to help her in the past but he did not help after seeing how violent she became when the accused man threatened to hit her.

Speaking after the case, she said, "I think it was just a game and we went into it. It was one of those things we both started doing. It just went too far."

Judge Richard Hone QC told the pair, "You were both in this together. You had taken part in this sadistic act. It was a brutal and deliberate attempt to deprive your victim of her life.

Khanzadeh Momeni, defending, said both men were of "young, attractive characters".

"It is a tragic and tragic case," he said. "In our society if one of many acts of violence is committed as part of the game it can be described as a crime.

"However, this is such a shocking and tragic case that the circumstances of this case will have to be looked at in a new light.

"The defence case is that they are innocent."

'Mixed emotions'

On behalf of the prosecution, Nick Paget QC put forward three scenarios of what happened, all based on evidence the defence would have been able to produce.

The first involved a "game gone wrong".

He told the court it suggested the girl was lured into the first bedroom of her home, where the accused men were present, by offers of drugs or alcohol.

In fact she had been lured in through their friend, the court heard.

Then there was the second scenario, where the accused man suggested their friend threatened to beat him up, the court heard. However, it was the girl who suggested they go to his bedroom and the prosecution said the accused men had been present when they went in.

Mr Paget said the prosecution thought that scenario was the most likely, pointing out the "mixed emotions" that were on display in court.

There is no suggestion their friend had any involvement in his victim's death.

Choosing the right cup for your beverage can be a personal preference, as different brands and types of coffee or tea can offer distinct qualities, aromas, and tastes. The type of tea used can impact the flavor, thickness, and burn of the finished drink, while the type of coffee can influence how it is prepared.

What is a Coffee Device?

A coffee device is a tool that prepares hot liquids by boiling water to the ideal temperature, allowing for a fresh cup of coffee. Coffee and tea are composed of various elements (coffee, water, grounds), and a coffee device simply boils the mixture to create a rich cup of coffee.

Early Coffee Devices

One of the first types of coffee devices to enter the home was a stove-top model designed for home kitchens. It was a simple and convenient device that worked well for many people and led to mass-produced versions soon after. This device has a stove-top setting, a steam-injected heating element, and a coffee maker chamber, allowing it to boil water and coffee together for the best flavor. Other models are more basic, typically containing only a steam-injected heating element and a coffee maker chamber, with a lower quality of product.

Variations of Coffee Devices

There are many types of coffee devices available, and you may want to consider the type of setup for your current brewing setup. Depending on how you want to prepare your tea or coffee, you may need to add different devices to your coffee or tea kit. In this section, we will explore the differences between stove-top coffee devices, simple espresso machines, and modern, high-end electric models.

Stove-Top Coffee Devices

Stove-top coffee devices have been around for over a century and come in various forms, including electric, stove-top, and electric steam devices. All stove-top models use boiling water to prepare tea or coffee, with some featuring a single water reservoir below the brew button and others having multiple reservoirs for hot or cold water. You will also need to prepare the water yourself, which allows for the cost of an electric unit.

Stovetop Espresso Machines

A stovetop espresso machine combines steaming, steam, and grinding capabilities to quickly prepare coffee. These machines are designed to produce great flavors, as the steaming, steam, or grinding functions combine to create the best flavor.

Modern Espresso Machines

A modern stovetop espresso machine uses a steam filter that prevents the water from contacting the coffee grounds, allowing for optimal steamed coffee. The steam filter is typically a plastic device that sits inside the steamer basket.

Electric Espresso Machines

An electric espresso machine uses heat to prepare espresso using a steam-pressure method. The steam pressures created while brewing the coffee are high enough to force the water and grounds through the filter and into the beverage chamber. These machines are also called "electric" and have similar features when used with hot or cold water.

Electric Espresso Machines vs. Steam Espresso Machines

A steam machine allows the water to steam through the heated brew basket, creating high pressure and a strong brew. An electric espresso machine uses hot water and steam pressure to brew coffee, allowing for the best taste without boiling the coffee or wasting flavor. This is often the preferred method of brewing espresso and is considered "old school".

The concept of "districting" is a crucial aspect of determining which political parties win or lose in elections. While we have become familiar with the art of political districting, there are several ways to prevent it. Two simple strategies can be employed.

One strategy is to allow citizens to vote on the district lines. This approach has been used by many states for over 100 years. Additionally, some states have made it a constitutional requirement.

To achieve this, citizens can vote directly for state officials or for representatives. The goal is to ensure that district lines are drawn to represent the interests of a diverse cross-section of American society, rather than just urban areas. Representatives must represent the diverse population and values of their constituents.

A "consensus district plan" is needed, where every citizen in the district knows exactly what their vote means. When drawing these maps, fairness principles should be followed.

In this article, I will argue for a "consensus plan" that follows fairness principles. I will suggest four fair-shading principles that should guide districting plans across the country. I will also suggest that districts with different fair-shading principles will allow Democrats to win an extra 3 to 4 seats in Congress compared to the current congressional map.

The process of creating new congressional districts and the laws governing districting are not clearly understood. However, it is believed to be an art form, like chess, and a way to ensure that congressional lines are drawn to favor one party or another.

Our current districting system can be thought of as a chess game. Imagine a player on the board, designated by the state, who decides which state will host each congressional district based on population differences between each state.

The game starts with each state producing its own fair-shading map. The goal is to draw "neutral" fair-shading, where districts are drawn to ensure the total number of residents in each district is close to the state population.

We'll call this an equal population district, and it's easy to compare fair-shading designs. The player must choose a district with 100% alike residents.

Fairness is not only about drawing districts that look the same, but also about drawing districts that are even or more even than normal. This means drawing a "normal" district by simply counting the total residents.

In political science, this is called "equal population." It's the only way to draw a perfectly equal population district. All other methods leave a "gaping gap" between districts.

We can calculate the size of the gaps, for example, by dividing the overall population of a district by 12 and dividing it by the number of citizens.

In the real world, districts would be drawn without gaps because any state could meet the needs of all citizens.

A recent investigation has uncovered a significant connection between environmental pollution and depression. Additionally, the rate of suicide is a crucial indicator of depression, particularly depression resulting from the loss of someone dear.

The study, conducted in collaboration with the National Institute of Health and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, analyzed the correlation between the two and discovered that the higher the level of environmental pollution, the greater the likelihood of depression.

Dr. Susan F. Petroni, lead author and professor of psychiatry and behavioral sciences at the University of Cambridge, has previously stated:

"There is mounting evidence suggesting that exposures to environmental chemicals, both natural and man-made, may trigger depression and contribute to suicide. This is the result of the association between suicide and environmental exposure."

"There is no clear scientific consensus on these concerns," Petroni continues. "We believe that environmental causes of mental disorders, and their impact on public health, should be a central concern for health researchers and policymakers."

In their study, researchers compiled data from the National Epidemiologic Survey on Alcohol and Related Conditions, a longitudinal study that has tracked the health and behavior of over 25,000 U.S. adults since 1975. Additionally, they compiled population data through 2012 regarding "depressive disorders."

Over the course of the study, researchers found that people who live in the U.S. have "a higher rate of depressive disorders" than those who live in other developed countries (4.1 percent compared to a reported 1.1 percent in the U.S.). The study's investigators point out that when this was combined with the fact that suicide is the second leading cause of death in the U.S., researchers found that "the rate of depression-related suicide attempts in the U.S. may be higher for every fifth suicide patient than for non-suicidal patients."

"Depressive disorders are among the most common mental disorders in the U.S., with rates at 20-40 percent of the general population," it continues.

In order to determine the environmental factors that led to these high rates of depression, researchers turned their attention to an environmental hazard that would be of highest concern to all Americans—pollution. They found that there was a "strong association" between suicide and air pollution "particularly in cities, large towns, or metropolitan areas with high concentrations," and "low levels or very low concentrations of ozone and fine particulate matter."

Furthermore, the researchers found that these environmental causes of depression "were not limited to particular occupational categories, such as pollution. For instance, people living in the same census tracts in the same cities with high average levels of pollution were no more likely to be depressed than those in areas with lower pollution levels."

"A few of them may be more hazardous to health, but overall the association is very strong. We don't see the sort of broad exposure to environmental factors that is typical of epidemiological samples of this kind."

However, not everyone is convinced. There are a number of reasons why researchers believe that pollution and mental health could not be the only factors that influence the link between pollution and depression. The first is that the study, at this point, only examined "depressive disorders" and "suicide attempts." There were no data on "environmental exposure" as being the cause of these events; no data was collected on the types of sources that led to these environmental exposures. For instance, is it possible that these environmental triggers were not the kind of environmental triggers that most Americans would encounter but were more of a "trigger" that only occurs in certain areas?

The second is that research indicates that exposure to environmental chemicals doesn't necessarily produce this type of depression, but that it creates these conditions. For instance, scientists in Australia have observed that environmental chemicals have been found in the urine of deceased people, but the chemicals themselves have not been identified as the cause. The scientists, however, are looking to see if these chemicals could be linked to certain types of cancers. These chemicals would likely be considered carcinogens; they are thought to create inflammation in the body, which could contribute to cancer.

"If we can find something in the environment that is not a carcinogen but induces inflammation, that's an area that we really need to look at," Petroni said.

The third factor is the fact that the relationship between environmental pollution and depression could be due to the fact that other mental illnesses are often treated with drugs. "If you look at depression in terms of the number of treatments people take, it's not surprising that we're seeing more and more people taking these types of drugs," she said.

The scent of a significant divide within the Conservative leadership contest has begun to waft.

Insiders close to the party reveal that Calgary MP Michael Chong has renounced his registration to sign up as a delegate ahead of the Conservative nominating convention in Saskatoon, a move they claim is a protest against the leadership.

The news of Chong's decision to re-register was initially reported by Terry Milewski of the CBC.

In an email dated October 3, Chong penned a letter to party officials, tendering his resignation and requesting a delegate position.

However, within an hour of sending his email, Chong and his campaign team decided to rescind his resignation and re-register as a candidate – a move they have since repeated.

Chong's campaign chairman, Mark Northmullen, told Milewski that Chong's motivation is to demonstrate his commitment to working with whoever emerges as the Conservative party leader.

The former MP will attend the Saskatoon convention to connect with Conservatives he has worked with in the community and within the party's federal wing.

Chong gained notoriety as a political maverick, repeatedly challenging Prime Minister Stephen Harper and later leading a successful bid for the leadership of a third party.

However, Chong has faced significant political setbacks.

Chong has been under investigation by the Royal Canadian Mounted Police for alleged misuse of public funds, and he was charged with breach of trust in relation to lobbying federal government officials to approve the construction of a multi-million dollar home on a property he did not own.

This case remains ongoing.

Chong was also fined $20,000 and ordered to pay $30,000 in legal costs by a judge. Chong did not appeal this decision.

Chong stated last year that he had no intention of dropping out of the race, stating he would attend the Saskatoon convention with as many delegates as possible and was confident the party leadership race would produce a clear winner.

However, when Harper launched his assault on the Reform party, Chong removed his name from his campaign headquarters, informing party members he would not campaign as part of a Conservative-led coalition.

In a letter to Conservative activists this July, Chong stated while he did not formally announce his decision not to seek the Tory leadership, he had concluded he was no longer interested in running in the contest.

After the Conservative convention in Saskatoon, Chong told his supporters he was "prepared and willing" to run again in the next round of leadership campaigns – and would be available to assist the Conservative parties across the country should any Conservative member ever request it.

In a statement released Tuesday morning, Chong's federal director, Brian Sibley, described the move as "a political gesture to demonstrate his support for whoever becomes the Conservative leader."

Sibley stated Chong is still "very much in the race" and still believes he can secure a victory in the race to succeed Harper.

"He was certainly in contact with the party leadership team to determine whether he wanted to re-register or not before deciding to resign himself. He was aware that in his capacity as a candidate he needed to be cautious about how he could conduct himself," he said.

The decision by Chong to register himself as a candidate means he can participate in any candidate debate.

According to The Canadian Press, Chong's decision comes after he was blocked from participating in the CBC's leadership debate last week.

A Conservative source tells the Toronto Star that Chong's decision puts pressure on candidates to join him if they wish to participate in the Conservative leadership debate.

Be sure this is the SerialPort.open() line. If your serial port does not support this call then use Arduino-specific syntax to connect your Arduino.

The serial port is also used to send data to your computer. Use a program called "Serial Monitor" (link to your hardware) to see the details of the flow of your data on your Serial Port.

If your Mac is an old or current model, you don't have to use Arduino IDE. You will need to use the Serial Terminal application (link). This program can be installed by entering the terminal.app in the search box of your Mac. If you don't have the Terminal.app, you have an older Mac and need to find a copy of Terminal.app to install Terminal.app on your new Mac Model 10.5+.

Once you have found Serial Terminal, you will need to go to Applications ⇒ Utilities.

. In Utilities ⇒ Terminal, type the following:

sudo update-alternatives --config terminal

Enter the terminal and hit return. The terminal will show you the current list of possible options to choose from. Enter one of the following options:

sudo update-alternatives --config compton

sudo update-alternatives --config gtk-terminal

sudo update-alternatives --config python-terminal

To find which terminal can connect to your Arduino, enter this line into terminal:

osascript -e 'tell application "Terminal" to assign terminal="%SystemRoot%\System32\Terminal.app" '

You may need to restart the terminal to see the change take effect.

To see a list of terminal applications on your computer, enter this:

ls -l /Applications

The Terminal.app in /Applications is a default desktop applet which allows your computer to be accessed without pressing a key or mouse button.

If you don't know the current version of your Terminal applet enter this:

ls -l /Applications /Applications

The following commands will let you add Terminal.app to your default programs list:

sudo update -h now

sudo add-apt-repository ppa:grafik/terminal sudo apt-get update


The next line will let you remove Terminal.app from your defaults:

sudo apt-get remove terminal

To add Terminal.app to your customizations go to Preferences ⇒ System ⇒ Advanced and open the Terminal panel. Find Terminal.app and click the Add button. Enter the URL below and hit return.

Once this process is complete, you will probably want to restart your computer.

To see the details of Terminal.app's connection to your computer, enter this:

sudo nano /usr/bin/terminal

Enter the following:

#!/bin/bash

x=""

while [ "$x" -ne "$x" ]; do

case "$x" in

"$1" |

"*" |

"*)") print x;;

esac

done

The first option simply loops while the switch doesn't evaluate to false.

The second statement creates a loop (with one case) that keeps repeating the code until x evaluates to not empty. (This is similar to a while loop. The difference is in this statement, we create an infinite (for loop). This is done to create an infinite loop that doesn't terminate until it completes a cycle. The only thing this would terminate would be if you typed the string x.)

"*" |

"*)") print x;;

esac

done

I couldn't justify continuing when the pay wasn't enough for a small apartment in central Seattle.

I also had my work schedule dictated by my parents, which kept me going when I tried to quit my job.

The second company seemed similar but didn't feel like I had complete creative control.

I decided I didn't want to just work like an intern, so I decided to take one last shot at finishing a book while working on my blog.

This decision ultimately led me to where I am today.

* 4-5 garlic cloves, finely minced
* 1 tsp salt
* ½ tsp black pepper
* ½ tsp olive oil, plus additional for drizzling

3. Cook for 4 people, with each person requiring approximately ⅓ of the sauce.

Method:

3. Remove from the slow cooker and serve over pasta.

A recent study of American Jewish individuals revealed that many hold concerns regarding the Islamic faith, while others perceive no distinction between the United States and Israel. American Jewry is becoming increasingly secular, with secular Jews expressing growing anxiety about their faith and confidence in Israel's future.

The survey, conducted by the Pew Research Center's Forum on Religion & Public Life, also discovered that American Jews prioritize personal feelings over communal concerns:

A majority of American Jews (60%) believe their Jewish identity does not impact their emotions regarding their future in Israel.

A similar majority (63%) believe the strength of Israel's democracy enhances Jewish life globally.

The same percentage (66%) believes a Jewish state is not a viable option for Israel today, despite 77% of Jews in Israel holding the opposite view.

Almost all American Jews (96%) do not consider Israel's national identity relevant to their Jewish life in the United States.

American Jews also reported being less interested in politics and government than the general American population. A full 87% do not watch the news, and 71% do not take action on political issues. Only 17% have ever made a political campaign donation.

Individuals who perceive little conflict between Judaism and Israel are more likely to see tension between Judaism and Israel. In this case, American Jews are divided: 42% believe American Jews should advocate more for Jewishness in Israel, while 44% disagree.

The survey asked American Jews who do not see conflict between Judaism and Israel what they would do if the United States became more secularized. More than two-thirds of the American Jewish population believe this would not be a positive development for Jews in America. This sentiment is not unique to American Jews; 68% of Jews in Israel believe there will be a conflict between Israel's identity as a Jewish and democratic state and the Jewishness of its Jewish citizens.

When asked what American Jews can do to preserve the Jewishness of the State of Israel, 72% believe being involved in the American Jewish community is crucial, while 68% believe making Jewish life in Israel better for Jews worldwide is essential. The same percentage would support the Boycott Divestment Sanction movement.

The survey presented findings in a breakdown of American Jews according to two dimensions of American-Jewish identity: the political and the religious.

Political and religious self-identification

American Jews do not perceive significant conflict between Judaism and Israel: Nearly two-thirds believe there will be a conflict between Israel's identity as a Jewish and democratic state and the Jewishness of its Jewish citizens, according to the poll.

However, a growing number of American Jews see less conflict between Judaism and Israel.

According to the poll, roughly a third of American Jews believe being Jewish does not impact their identity and future in Israel.

Only 16% of American Jews – just two points more than the 22% who do not consider Israel's national identity relevant to their Jewish life in the United States – take seriously the idea that their religious identity is at odds with their secularized lifestyle in the United States.

Meanwhile, American Jews are more than twice as likely to be involved in the community than Jews in Israel.

The Supreme Court recently deliberated on the Obergefell v. Hodges case, which could establish a national definition of marriage. The justices appeared divided on two key issues: how to categorize gay individuals and whether states can prohibit same-sex unions without compromising their current rights. The discussion primarily focused on gay couples and transgender individuals. 

Conservative Justice Anthony Kennedy and liberal Justice Stephen Breyer both advocated for a same-sex couple's right to marry and adopt children, just like heterosexual couples. They are correct, but also misguided in their views on the opposing side. Marriage was and is meant for a specific purpose, and gay people should not be treated differently. If the decision were solely about the constitutional right to marriage, it would be straightforward. It's not; it's about the dignity of gay individuals, equality, and the moral right to be treated equally. 

For the first time, gay people will have the same legal right to marry as heterosexuals. They will enjoy the same legal benefits and parental rights. Through marriage, gay people can live full lives in harmony with other human beings, avoiding marginalization. 

The decision is significant not only for gay individuals but for their children and grandchildren. Children raised by gay parents tend to be more tolerant of other cultures and religious diversity. 

The Supreme Court should overturn the court of appeals' decision and affirm same-sex couples' constitutional right to marry. This would be the only decision, and it would be a significant public stand. 

If these decisions were affirmed, history could look very different. We are fortunate to live in a country where the democratic process is guided by the First Amendment and the 14th Amendment, which guarantees equal protection under the law. 

The court of appeals' decision would still permit states to prohibit same-sex couples from marrying. However, a state might not be able to ban all gay couples in the state from doing so. This would be called a "compelling state interest" and an appeal would go to the Supreme Court. 

With the same ruling, the court of appeals would have upheld the federal Defense of Marriage Act, denying benefits to same-sex spouses of federal employees. If that law were upheld, the Obama administration would have to recognize same-sex marriages in those states, leaving gay couples without domestic partnership benefits. 

If the court decides to do nothing, the Supreme Court or the court of appeals would have upheld Proposition 8 as constitutional, banning the state of California from recognizing gay marriages and same-sex couples from adopting children. If a different court found Proposition 8 unconstitutional, then marriage could be defined as the legal union between one man and one woman.

Another promise that rings true is that the United States will see a more open market for business in general. A fascinating enigma surrounds the emergence of America as a leader in defense and law enforcement. It's as if a unique convergence of circumstances led to the development of innovative solutions. 

In 1765, the renowned English scientist Sir Humphry Davy presented his groundbreaking invention to the Royal Society of London. The society was considering patenting gunpowder, and Davy had been informed that they were doing so. Following the society's approval of the patent, Davy received a mysterious message and a note from an unknown individual, claiming the society was no longer relevant and that gunpowder would never be patented in the United States.

Davy's autobiography mentions the encounter, describing the unknown individual as an old man who had known him for twenty years. The individual claimed to have only two sons and was a poor man. This encounter sparked the notion that a single person could ignite the first explosion in human history.

The "just one person" theory is plausible, as seen in the case of engineer J.E.D. McDonald, who died in 1837 while attempting to invent a high-powered gas-powered rocket. McDonald's rocket remained on a shelf at his company for three years before being taken by someone else.

Another theory suggests that Davy himself could be the unknown individual. It's possible that Davy learned about the unpatented metallurgy from his former colleague and decided to wait until he was older to invent a bomb.

Theories about Davy's involvement in the mysterious meeting of the Royal Society have been debated for nearly 150 years. In 1955, British historian and chemist Sir Robert Watson-Watt conducted a three-year study, visiting the National Archives in London. He discovered that the society's first gunpowder patent, issued on December 17, 1762, contained a line stating that Davy had a patent granted by the Royal Society of London. This raised questions about Davy's claim to be the inventor of gunpowder.

A more plausible explanation emerged from a July 17, 1761 meeting of the Committee of Correspondence, where Davy discussed patent applications with another scientist, Robert Bunsen. In the meeting minutes, Bunsen referred to Davy as the "most extraordinary person we have ever met." He advised Davy to patent new metallurgy, as someone else would if he didn't.

Bunsen's next meeting with the society was on September 17, 1766, just a month after Davy received the mysterious telegram. In the minutes from that meeting, Bunsen agreed that if his plan failed, Davy could try again with his new "chemical furnace."

The evidence surrounding Davy's involvement in gunpowder is extensive. In July 1782, Thomas Harriot presented a paper to the Royal Society, claiming that French scientists had invented gunpowder, and that English scientists, including Davy, had created the same chemical. Harriot's "proof" was the ingredients needed to make gunpowder, as outlined in a 1764 patent for an invention that would later become known as Deutz-Fahrzeug.

A significant issue in healthcare settings is the development of infections associated with central venous catheters. These infections, often referred to as CLABSIs, occur when microorganisms enter the body through a long, thin tube inserted into a vein. Central venous catheters are frequently used for medication administration, fluid delivery, or blood sampling. CLABSIs can be severe and potentially life-threatening, as they can lead to sepsis. Common indicators of a CLABSI include fever, chills, redness or swelling around the insertion site, and changes in the catheter's appearance. To minimize the risk of CLABSIs, healthcare professionals should adhere to proper hand hygiene, infection control practices, and aseptic technique when inserting or caring for central venous catheters. Additionally, they should ensure proper catheter maintenance and removal when no longer needed. Patients should be aware of the signs and symptoms of a CLABSI and report any concerns to their healthcare provider.

The conflict at hand was not solely about slavery, but rather the struggle for land and secession. The South sought to secure its economic future by controlling the land, while the North aimed to prevent this from occurring.

However, the North did not concur, with most northerners seeking to abolish the slavery system, which was the root of much suffering in the South. Following the war, a new nation emerged, with a republic rather than a constitutional republic, resulting in the United States being split.

Upon the war's conclusion, the Confederacy remained the only slave nation in America. Slaves enjoyed legal rights and privileges comparable to those of their owners, with the Confederate constitution mirroring those of the antebellum South.

The Confederacy's foundation was rooted in slavery and the belief that blacks should not be allowed citizenship in the United States. Secessionists argued that the Confederacy was born from this conviction.

Many Americans believed that allowing blacks to vote would be unconstitutional, as states cannot deny citizenship to citizens. However, the southern states did not agree, fearing that granting blacks the right to vote would lead to demands for equal political rights with whites.

The Confederacy sought to prevent citizens of the South from voting, as this would have resulted in greater integration of blacks and whites in American society, which was unacceptable to Confederate leaders who did not want blacks to mingle with whites in a white-dominated society.

Some historians argue that the Southern secessionist leaders' desire for increased racial segregation led to their fight against Jim Crow laws in the North. However, this assertion is incorrect, at least in the eyes of the Southern Confederates.

In addition, blacks had little to no representation by white politicians and businessmen in the South.

All these laws were enacted specifically to exclude blacks from government positions.

The Confederate's fear of increased racial mixing was so intense that they also supported laws prohibiting blacks from having the same voting rights as whites. While their concern that a black voter would influence a legislator's decisions was understandable, it did not justify these laws. His companion inquired about my mode of transportation, and I explained it was a "novelty" vehicle. The gentleman offered some words of wisdom, stating that this was the reason I possessed such a vehicle.

Following the incident, I penned a letter to the gentleman, detailing the significant transformations that had occurred in my life.

My father, who had recently passed away, had also made a name for himself in his community. This was during a time when there was a significant campaign against same-sex marriage in California.

However, I, who had relocated to New York and am now in my 40s, assert that the passage of Proposition 184 did not alter my identity. I continued to live life as openly as possible, and I continued to be as authentic as possible.

The letter was published on a website dedicated to personal stories, where I share my experiences as a teenager and young adult. I also maintain a daily blog where I discuss various topics, including my thoughts on personal identity.

Writing about these experiences brings me a sense of catharsis. It allows me to process my emotions and reflect on my journey.

The letters I wrote to my father are included in the article, which chronicles my experiences in high school, college, and beyond.

Although I don't explicitly claim to be straight, the letters are written from a personal perspective that explores my identity.

The stories also include descriptions of my relationships, which suggest that I felt the need to conform to societal expectations.

"I was extremely afraid of being myself," I write. "The only way I could fit in was to be the kind of person who was perceived as being effeminate."

In one instance, I wrote, "I was so close to losing my mind."

However, I have come to realize that my relationships and the changes that led me to leave were "more successful than I could have ever imagined."

"I learned to embrace my true self," I write. "I learned to be my authentic self, which is gay."

In my letter to the gentleman, I explained how I have come to terms with my sexuality.

"I am gay because I am created to be gay," I write. "I am gay because God loves me, and I am gay because God has created me to be gay."

In response to the gentleman's questioning of my sexuality, I wrote that I am a "fearful gay individual" who has "a lot of guilt."

"There are people who have given me a hard time, whether straight or gay," I write. "What I've learned from it and am working out now is that nobody is to blame. This isn't about them."

However, I also write, "I know who you are. I know who you are not. I can see what you've become. You know you're not alone in this."

I was contacted by a journalist on Wednesday to discuss my letter, but I was unavailable to respond.

A package has several classes. The classes are categorized into three main categories. The first category is the default class. This class is used in all packages. The second category is the "lightweight" class. This class was introduced in the 1.0 release and will be used in the 1.2.x release. The third category is the "normal" class.

The "normal" class is divided into three subclasses. The first subclass is used directly by this package. The second subclass is used by all other packages. The third subclass is used by this package.

There are also other classes. The first class is never used. It is for convenience only. The second class is also never used. It is for convenience only. The third class is a synonym for the second class.

For example, the "normal" class can be used like this:

>>> from package import Normal
Normal: 
pass
>>> normal = Normal()
>>> normal.a = 3
>>> normal <class 'Normal'>
>>> normal.b = 7
>>> normal.c = 5
>>> normal.a 6
>>> Normal() # Normal class has no attributes.
Normal() # Normal class has no attributes.
>>> from package import Normal2
normal2 = Normal2(10)
>>> normal2 <class 'Normal'>
>>> normal2.b 7
>>> normal2 <class 'Normal2'>

Class definitions may have attributes. For a class declaration, this is just an index. For a class instance, this is the "class property".

Class instances are "global".

For example, the attributes of a class object are the "instance" objects:

>>> from package.abc import ABC
ABC.object = 42
>>> ABC.object.a 1
>>> ABC.object.b 43
>>> A = ABC(object)
>>> A.object.a 43
>>> class A:
... pass
>>> a = A()
>>> a <__main__.A object at 0x1f8dc0f8>

Class instances do not follow any attributes of the class. This includes class attributes, attributes that are part of the class's class attributes when it is a normal or lightweight class, and attributes that are attributes on a class instance itself.

class A: 
pass
>>> r = A()
>>> r
>>> r.object.a # an attribute from instance class (A)
>>> r.object.b None
>>> r.object.c None
>>> r.c.class_instance([])
>>> r <__main__.A object at 0x1f8dc0f8>
>>> r.object.a 2
>>> r.object.b 5

This works for normal and lightweight classes.

For "heavyweight" classes, objects do not inherit attributes from the class. This is because the weight of a class is determined by its instances (which are simply instances of the class).

class A: 
... pass
>>> a = A()
>>> a class A: 
... pass
>>> a2 = A()
>>> a2 class A: 
... pass
>>> a <__main__.A object at 0x1f8dc0f8>

There is no "instance" attribute on a normal class, only attributes from classes.

class T(): 
pass
>>> class D(): 
pass
>>> d = D()
>>> d.object.class_instance(T) # the normal class has no attributes.
D() # the normal class has no attributes.
>>> d.object.a 1
>>> d.object.b None

For "lightweight" classes, there is one attribute for class instances:

>>> class A(object): 
pass
>>> a = A()
>>> a[0] 2
>>> a.object.a # there is an instance attribute for A (which corresponds to a)
A() # there is an instance attribute for A (which corresponds to a)

The attribute is called object, and represents the class (instance) object.

pass

pass

pass

D() # similar to D.class_instance(A.object)

The findings were published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.

A stalwart of the Minnesota Vikings' defensive line, Bob Kehoe still reminisces about his college days with a certain Chris Culliver, now a force to be reckoned with on the San Francisco 49ers' defense. Their bond is forged in the crucible of competition.

"Those warriors are unyielding," Kehoe reflected recently. "They'll unleash their full fury upon you. You must never underestimate their mettle. It will be a daunting task to contain Chris, not to mention the rest of the team."

Kehoe, a veteran of the University of South Florida's gridiron, recalled a memorable encounter with Culliver at the University of Virginia. When asked to deliver a passage from the "Famous Quotations of Winston Churchill," Culliver surprised Kehoe with the phrase "You never need weapons except when there are none." This pithy remark has since become known as "closing the barn door after the horse has bolted," but Kehoe explained its significance with tongue-in-cheek. Culliver regaled Kehoe with the quote's origins.

"If you possess a team with one exceptional player, but lack the necessary tools to execute on the field, that's when problems arise. So, he shared this wisdom," Kehoe chuckled.

Kehoe mused, "It's true that you can't have one exceptional player without the right tools to succeed on offense. In college, however, they had an abundance of talent. The defensive players would be primed for action."

Culliver, a star quarterback in his college days, threw for over 3,000 yards in each of his final three seasons.

"He's like a brother to me," Kehoe said. "His story is nothing short of remarkable, and we've been close for many years. It was amusing when we faced the Packers, as he was playing on injured reserve. It wasn't a significant issue to get him back in the lineup. Yet, I hold him in the highest esteem – and that quote was an affront to him. He deserves immense credit and respect for his dedication to the game."

Culliver, well-acquainted with Kehoe, is also familiar with his professional basketball endeavors. Kehoe played 10 years in the NBA with the Indiana Pacers, earning the respect of coaches like Tom Thibodeau.

In a recent meeting, a colleague remarked, "You've faced tougher challenges." Kehoe thought to himself, "Tom really went over the top in his criticism of me."

However, Kehoe added, "Earlier, Tom was the most prominent coach, known for his interviews and news appearances. Then, he became a head coach, and I thought, 'Wow, he's transformed as a coach.' But that got caught in the crossfire when he was let go. It's truly a shame, as I've had the chance to know him as a person – a good guy who's been successful in the NBA, an All-American, and a successful businessman."

Culliver, 27, is known for his on-field prowess and off-field controversies. He's won the Defensive Rookie of the Year Award four times, the Defensive Player of the Year Award twice, and the NFL's Defensive Player of the Year Award with the Cincinnati Bengals in 2010.

Culliver, signed to a six-year, $45 million contract in March, has been one of the most versatile defenders in the NFL since his arrival in 2012. He can rush from the edge, play inside, and excel in both the nickel and dime packages.

This season, Culliver is playing all five downs for the Chiefs. As a pass-rusher, he leads the NFL with 17.5 sacks and a league-best 13.5 sacks this season.

"There was no more dominant pass-rusher this year than him," Vikings quarterback Teddy Bridgewater said during a postgame interview. "He's like an older version of the young Joe Flacco, always seeking to sack the quarterback."

In this guide, I'll cover the two most essential aspects of any player's character.

1) Vitality, and 2) Potency.

1) Vitality

Vitality is your character's vital energy. This is represented by a numerical value displayed at the top of your screen. There are four levels that this is scaled to. When you are full, you will not regain vitality until your energy is depleted. Depending on how far you are away from a rejuvenation station, your vitality will drop further and possibly dwindle if there is no station within walking distance. Your vitality is displayed in your character's profile, and also increases over time. Your vitality is represented by a vitality bar, which is used in various ways. It can be activated with a key or the analog stick, and when activated, your character gains additional resilience. (Note: I have not tested this with a mouse. If it works, it would be fascinating. If not, it would be inconvenient.)

To attack, your character will hold down the attack (default L3). When you are holding down the attack, you have unlimited potent attacks. However, you are also limited in how far you can attack. Potent combos work as described in the following section.

If the action button is pressed in the same direction as the analog pad at the same time, then a potent combo (default R3) or a special (default Square) attack can be activated in that direction. Also, with Square, a potent or special can be activated even if you are facing away from the action button, as long as the analog stick is in the correct position. (Note: you don't always have to press the action button in the direction of the motion stick. Sometimes you can hit an action button and then hold the analog stick down again, and then hit the potent or special.) When you do use special attacks or potencies, you cannot cancel them.

You have 10 vital energy levels, which gradually decrease by half over time. When you get hit, you go into a stunned state, and will recover to full vitality over time. If you have more than 10 vital energy levels, you cannot use any other special attacks or potencies. If you lose more than 10 vital energy levels, or you have less than 10 vital energy remaining, you expire. If you have less than 5 vital energy remaining, it is possible to revive after expiring as long as you have at least one vital energy level left. You may be able to revive up to 5-10 times (depending on the character and level) at a vitality station, located in the middle of the map where vitality stations spawn. Note: If you have 10 or more vital energy, you will be automatically revived when you start expiring.

Also, your vitality regen does not get turned off while in a stunned state or unconscious. If you are stunned, or unconscious and fall below zero vitality, your vitality regen gets turned off immediately. Your remaining vitality (the fraction) is returned over time, and your vitality bar is restored when you get back up.

2) Potency

Potency is your character's current vitality. It begins at zero and progresses up through a number of vital energy levels at increasing potency. Each character starts off at level 1, and the potency they can deal is based on their level. However, it is not necessary to have a high potency in order to win a match. In fact, having low potency is an advantage. Your weapon selection can also play a large role in which weapon you are able to use.

Potency is displayed in your character's profile. Potency is displayed in a red bar, and the larger your bar is the faster your potency will progress. There is a specific way it is calculated that I have not talked about yet. For now, keep in mind that the more potency you have, the more you will increase your overall potency.

Potency increases while moving and your vitality regenerates while you are standing and/or breathing (no matter how tired you are). The amount of potency you can do at any time is equal to the amount of stamina in your stamina bar. When you have run out of stamina you will have to stop and recover vitality.

If you take potency (or a power or special attack) from a melee (or any other) weapon, you will take the same amount of potency and recover less. That is, if you take 5 potency from a sword and a pistol, you will recover 2 vitality. It takes two hits to kill a player even at level 6 with the default weapons.

3) Action List

You can customize which actions your character performs by pressing a button from this list. This list is also located in your profile. You may select which character you are currently controlling by hitting that character's symbol.

Your default weapon will be what you start out with (if you are playing with two characters, the one whose number is displayed will be your default character).

A new, high-speed train to link Beijing in China with the eastern edge of Tokyo has begun construction amid high-speed rail projects in the U.S. and Canada. (Reuters)

By Mieke Van Houtte and Paul Eckert

TOKYO — On a clear afternoon in early summer, the train hurtled across a wide expanse of green farmland around a hill in Tokyo's Shinagawa ward, a tony part of the city that was home to thousands of immigrants who fled Japan's economic downturn in the 1980s and '90s.

The train's interior was dark blue; its windows were tinted black, but passengers could see the green fields beyond, lit with the soft red glow of the sunset.

"Everyone just came out of the train and greeted the driver," a Chinese tourist with a smartphone recording the ride told his Japanese friend. "He said, 'Welcome to Tamao Station.' That's really nice for someone coming across from China, as much as they can be pleased to meet someone who speaks Japanese."

It was a typical Saturday afternoon commute, in a typical city that has seen an influx of foreign workers from China, and is expected to get much bigger. Prime Minister Shinzo Abe's conservative government is promoting high-speed train links, known as maglev, as a vital link to a revitalized economy battered by a sales-tax hike and a crippling earthquake, among other upheavals. There are nearly 300 people working in maglev development and testing at Tamao in Tokyo, and officials hope the trains will be operational well before the end of the decade.

But the train that the Chinese tourist encountered is a far cry from the glossy, futuristic concept that Japan is known for — and from a train that is, for the moment, still in the experimental phase.

I recall spending carefree days by the pool, where we'd take the plunge and splash around. My cousin, a pool enthusiast, once asked me how to keep teeth from falling out while playing. His mom, a dental student, thought I'd know the answer, but I just smiled and waved it off. She wasn't pleased.

"You'll have to learn to stay in the pool," she said, and I did. I went on to study at a reputable dental school in Cleveland, completed my residency, and started my practice in Baltimore. I became quite skilled, and my patients began asking for various treatments. To the general public, dental care is all about a radiant smile, but in reality, it's about teeth.

Many of my patients came from affluent families, having attended top-notch schools. They hadn't yet grasped that their teeth didn't define their success. They knew they didn't need to prioritize healthy eating and had the means to afford it. They were patient, and their teeth didn't require constant maintenance.

Recently, I met a wealthy patient who had crowns removed from his front teeth due to their severe crookedness, making it difficult for him to walk or drive. This struck a chord with me. I knew what he was saying was true, but I couldn't help feeling empathy.

I asked him, "Why do we let our mouths do all the work?" What are we doing to prevent this? The answer was obvious: good, old-fashioned eating, drinking, and avoiding detrimental foods. We stop prioritizing oral health around age six or seven.

However, the dental care industry has its own logic to keep teeth working hard. I was glad we discussed this with him, as it's crucial to understand the importance of good teeth. What are people doing if their dentist tells them to stay in their mouth until they're done? But what are they doing if their dentist says their teeth are like leaves on a tree? Are we not getting the most vital thing every person can do?

I've found a way to address this by educating my patients about good dental care, leading to healthier teeth and a greater sense of self-confidence. The message is clear: there's an alternative to neglecting our oral health.

The truth is, people need to be honest with themselves. I don't know what people are doing to their mouths, and that's fine. Talking to a doctor about it is also a good idea. We're all seeking answers that can bring about change.

The National Association for College Admission Counseling issued a statement urging the Department of Education to revisit its criteria for accepting transgender applicants. This move sparked debate, with some arguing that the existing guidance discriminates based on gender identity, while others claim it is insufficient.

Notably, the military's ban on LGBT troops does not impact how colleges and students receive federal student aid. The US Department of Education's Office for Civil Rights confirmed this, stating that the ban is unlikely to affect federal student aid.

For those unfamiliar with federal student debt, the federal government lends money to colleges through the federal financial aid program. Most federal student loans are private loans repaid through monthly installments. In cases where borrowers do not complete school or drop out, the government typically forgives the debt. The federal government covers various education-related costs, including book fees, room, and board.

The federal government also awards grants for education, including college tuition.

The Office for Civil Rights at the Department of Education emphasized that the federal government is not a borrower or grantor, stating that student loan repayment is the sole responsibility of the borrower. The federal government's role is to assist borrowers with college costs.

In response to a complaint filed by the American Civil Liberties Union of Illinois, the Office for Civil Rights asked the Department of Defense to clarify its ban on transgender service members and provide information on services offered, such as hormone treatments.

The Army revised its policy in February, citing outdated, discriminatory, and inconsistent reasoning. Military officials stated that under the new policy, all service members identifying as transgender will be treated as the gender with which they identify, potentially including medical treatments and surgeries paid for by the federal government.

Some colleges leverage the federal government to circumvent their own financial aid policies, as the federal government is prohibited from considering race, ethnicity, or religion when determining aid eligibility. In this instance, colleges have received funding through the federal financial aid program.

Drew Brees had a remarkable game, throwing 10 touchdown passes with no interceptions, completing 80.4% of his passes. The Saints' late touchdown run was a highlight, as Brees led the team to their second win with a late touchdown run.

In the realm of.NET, a common conundrum arises when multiple instances of the framework coexist, and the same libraries are required in both. My personal approach was to utilize two distinct.NET frameworks, one incorporating ASP.NET and the other leveraging Entity Framework. However, this issue can be tackled through alternative means, such as configuring a dependency manager and incorporating.NET assemblies into a container within your code. I opted to create a few compact assemblies, which serve as packages for the projects, ensuring their presence in both the.NET module (via a.NET assembly container) and the actual project (via a.MSIL assembly). The package comprises one or more assemblies, and it is crucial to place the package in the same folder as the assemblies in Visual Studio for it to function.

In this article, I will demonstrate how to achieve this using an external repository, a.NET configuration file, and the creation of those assemblies. I will leave the configuration file to your discretion and provide a link to a future post that will elaborate on its creation.

Employing the External Repository

The initial step is to generate the assemblies, or at least a few of them. For this tutorial, I will utilize an external repository called Nuget. The configuration for an external repository resembles the following:

<configuration> <add name = "Nuget.External.Microsoft.NuGet" /> <add name = "Nuget.External.Roslyn" /> <add name = "Nuget.External.CoreCLR.dll" /> <add name = "Nuget.External.SqlServer" /> <add name = "Nuget.External.System.Reflection.dll" /> </configuration>

The configuration file also contains information regarding the packages to be downloaded for convenience. I do not intend to utilize these packages, as the assemblies they define will not be installed by NuGet, which is an installer for packages in Visual Studio.

The packages I intend to utilize are listed as one or more assemblies within the configuration file. You can employ the dot (.) to delimit an assembly, or include a square bracket (`), which designates a full assembly name, such as "SqlServer.dll". If you are including an assembly in the configuration file for more than the three assemblies you will be utilizing, the file may expand to two or more lines.

Crafting the NuGet/Roslyn Packages

Initially, ensure that a new Microsoft.WindowsAzure.PowerShell.Core package is present in the NuGet package manager Console application. You will need to select this package as your development library in Visual Studio when configuring the package. Select the package in Visual Studio (and in the console as well) and navigate to the folder where you desire the assemblies to be located.

Next, create a file named "NuGet.config" in the folder where you desire the NuGet packages to be stored. For the purposes of this example, we will create a folder named "SqlServer." Now, create a new text file and name it "Roslyn.config" (without the final ".config" at the end of the file).

Add the following content to your Roslyn.config file: { "PackageKind": "Microsoft.WindowsAzure.PowerShell.Core", "ImportDependencyInPlace": false, "BuildConfiguration": { "GenerateProject": false, "EnableVisualStudioTargeting": false, "CompileNativeExtensions": true }, "SourceTargets": ["srcRootPath"], "AssemblyExtensions": "Microsoft.Net.SqlServer.SqlClient", }

The NuGet package management system requires some information to be known, as well as the package to be utilized. This information is contained within a configuration file written to disk, which defines what will be stored in the package cache. When a package is added to Visual Studio, it is first added to the NuGet package manager to cache its contents until the package is downloaded. The cache is a list of the packages the project will utilize, and the package cache can be substantial because it caches everything related to a package.

This next part includes one line of code:

// Create the Roslyn.Config file Microsoft.WindowsAzure.PowerShell.Core.Configuration.Create('Roslyn.config', 'C:\temp')

Pumpkin Delight

My little ones are absolutely enamored with the crust of pumpkin pie – especially! I had a few leftover recipes, so I whipped up a batch with a few tweaks. I began by using almost all of the ingredients from this crust. First of all, the fat that I used in the filling was skim milk, and the flour was whole wheat. This meant no cream cheese, instead I used a combination of butter and coconut oil in the crust. This resulted in a more tender crust, without the overly sweet pumpkin flavor. You get the full pumpkin flavor in the filling, so you don't need the coconut oil to help with that – which was nice. Next I also mixed in a cinnamon stick into my filling, instead of just adding it to the crust. It adds a little real pumpkin spice flavor.

Pumpkin Delight

3 tablespoons coconut oil

1/2 cup flour

1/2 cup sugar

1/2 teaspoon salt

4 tablespoons butter, cut into pieces

1/2 cup sugar

3 large eggs

3/4 cup buttermilk

1/2 teaspoon cinnamon

3 tablespoons melted butter, for topping

1 teaspoon vanilla extract

1 tablespoon milk, for whisking

1 8-ounce can pumpkin, drained and cut into 1/4 inch pieces

Preheat oven to 350 degrees F / 180 degrees C. Line an 8-inch pie pan with parchment paper. Combine coconut oil and flour in a bowl and mix until smooth. (I just used a wooden spoon.) Add sugar. Add salt. Mix until combined. Combine butter and sugar in a large bowl. Add eggs, and mix until combined. Add buttermilk, cinnamon and melted butter as well as the eggs and buttermilk. Mix until just combined. Set aside. In a separate shallow bowl, whisk together the milk and butter. Set aside. In the same bowl that you mixed eggs/butter for, mix together buttermilk, flour, and cinnamon. Add mixture to the bowl with eggs and buttermilk. Turn dough out onto a lightly floured surface and knead for 10 minutes or until dough is smooth. Shape into large, oval shape that is 3/4 inch thick – it will be slightly thicker than a quarter. Place dough in prepared pie pan and cover with parchment paper for up to 1 hour. After the first hour, remove pie from the oven and allow it to fully cool. Once it is cool enough to handle, press dough firmly down using a fork to prevent it from sliding around.

When you are ready to bake it, remove the parchment paper and place the pie over a baking sheet so it is almost level with the bottom edge of the sheet. Grease the back of the pie plate with coconut oil and then place pie on top of the coconut oil. Bake for 30 to 40 minutes or until golden. Allow to cool on a wire rack before cutting.

A recent analysis by Robert Gordon of Northwestern University and Emmanuel Saez, now at the University of California, Berkeley, has shed new light on the intergenerational transmission of economic opportunity in advanced economies. The study found that inequality in the United States fell sharply during the decades before the financial crisis but has stabilized in the past ten years, even as the rest of the world's income has grown. The authors are concerned that the distribution of opportunities within the United States continues to widen as the rest of the world has become richer. To address this gap, the rich must be made to pay the same share of taxes as others.

Gordon and Saez discovered that the share of national income that went to the bottom 90 percent of earners has risen faster in the United States compared to other rich countries. However, this trend does not hold for the top 10 percent or even the top 1 percent of earners. The reason for this difference is that many countries have raised their taxes to fund the welfare state, thereby increasing the share of earnings going to the bottom 90 percent.

The authors also noted that the increase in inequality has come even during the "great moderation," a period of rapid welfare state reform. However, it is not surprising that this happened because economic growth was weak, and countries had decades to implement reforms. In contrast, in the 1980s, the United States and other rich countries made the adjustment on their own.

When the United States raised its top tax rate from 50 percent to 70 percent in the 1980s, the richest one percent of earners accounted for a greater share of the overall pie than at any time since 1929. This change increased the share of overall income that went to the top earners considerably in the 1980s.

The United States's relative inequality is not only the highest in the OECD but may be quite high. The authors' measure of inequality shows that the share of income going to the bottom 90 percent fell even faster in the United States in the 1990s than it did in any other rich country. This implies that the United States has been getting more unequal as compared to other countries even with economic growth.

The authors emphasize the importance of controlling for other determinants of income distribution, such as technological change and differences in tax policies. However, the strong drop in inequality for the top 1 percent is not consistent with these other factors.

The world's oldest human, a majestic ruler of ancient Egypt, has been unearthed in a newly discovered burial site.

A senior government official revealed that the boy king and several generations of his family have been laid to rest in a vast cemetery, where thousands of mummies and artifacts are carefully arranged in rows.

Scholars are meticulously examining the burial chamber, constructed around 1350 BC, during the reign of the great pharaohs of Egypt's New Kingdom period.

Tutankhamun, the King of Upper and Lower Egypt, met his untimely demise in the 1220s BC.

His son, Akhenaten, rose to power in the 13th Century BC, only to be toppled by ancient rulers who deemed his cult worship idolatrous.

The discovery of Tutankhamun has sparked intense fascination about the circumstances surrounding his burial.

"I am both sorrowful and joyful," said Abdul-Aziz Ismail, the lead archaeologist on the site, upon uncovering the royal coffin and pharaoh's sarcophagus.

Archaeologists believe that Tutankhamun was interred on the west bank of the river, adjacent to his pyramid.

There is speculation that an attempt was made to relocate him from the chamber to an adjacent temple.

Some experts argue that the boy king was initially buried elsewhere and later moved to Akhenaten's tombs.

He was succeeded by a succession of pharaohs who ushered in a new golden age in Egypt, and was himself succeeded into the afterlife by his cousin Kiya.

According to ancient records, Kiya reigned for 1340 years and was also believed to be the son of Tutankhamun himself.

The tombs of kings were typically filled with mummified and partially mummified bodies of rulers.

The discovery of these tombs has provided a unique window into the past, offering a glimpse into royal funerary rites and customs.

For instance, scientists have recently uncovered a burial chamber at Tutankhamun's burial site to gain a deeper understanding of the boy king's life and times.

The newly discovered burial chamber is situated within the royal necropolis, constructed under the reign of Egypt's sixth pharaoh, Ramses the Great, around 1000 BC.

Archaeologists have located Tutankhamun's coffin, the body of his uncle Rameses II, and a mummy adorned with intricate tattoos.

Medicare estimates the total cost of services received by its beneficiaries over a period, adjusting the value of the service to determine reimbursement. Medicaid assumes no change in coverage and multiplies the cost by the beneficiary's income.

The difference between Medicaid and Medicare payments is zero. Both programs only pay for the most expensive and effective treatments. For example, they may cover a life-saving procedure but not the average cost, which is zero. This results in the same number of people receiving services without payment. The primary objective of Magic is achieving victory.

Victory [ edit | edit source ]

The ultimate goal is to accumulate the most cards in your hand within a predetermined timeframe. Certain sets may introduce additional victory conditions, such as eliminating the opponent's entire board or securing triumph from a specific card. These objectives can be combined to create a unique victory scenario.

For the purpose of this article, we will use the term "victory" to refer to the overall objective of accumulating the most cards in your hand.

Deck-building strategy revolves around selecting cards that facilitate victory. A deck-building strategy is a curated selection of cards that enhances the likelihood of winning.

Securing Victory with Creatures [ edit | edit source ]

If no specific objective is in mind, the most straightforward approach is to gain control over the board, eliminating the opponent's creatures or disrupting their playstyle. The key to success lies in gaining a significant card advantage before the opponent can respond. This can be achieved by deploying a creature that secures an insurmountable lead, such as an Aura or a small, formidable creature.

Securing Victory with Enchantments [ edit | edit source ]

Enchantments that force the opponent to lose are effective, but the opponent may counter your spell. If you have a counter, it's best to cast it before the opponent can respond. Sacrificing a permanent to counter a spell is often a viable option, but it's crucial to ensure the permanent is not tapped.

Securing Victory while Opposed [ edit | edit source ]

A common strategy involves creating a large horde of small creatures and then sacrificing most of them simultaneously. This forces the opponent to adapt to a more substantial deck, allowing you to gain an advantage. This approach is feasible even with limited mana, as the sheer number of small creatures can overwhelm the opponent.

Securing Victory in Unique Situations [ edit | edit source ]

If you're the sole player on a side of the board, the game is likely lost. You should either deter the opponent from joining you or focus on drawing cards to shift the board's momentum in your favor. Drawing cards can significantly alter the game's dynamics, and you're more likely to draw more cards as more players join the board.

Securing Victory in the Early/Mid Game [ edit | edit source ]

In the early or mid game, most opponents' cards are useless, and their decks are barren. You're more likely to have the right answers when you get there. This can occur by activating spells with a high chance of turning the game around without expending much mana or by creating a powerful creature that dominates the board.

Securing Victory in the Late Game [ edit | edit source ]

In the very late game, when the game is nearly unwinnable, it may be wise to focus on preventing opponents from playing their creatures. Drawing cards is always beneficial, but it's essential to use your resources prudently. For instance, if you're aware of an opponent's combo deck and they lack non-creature cards, it's best to draw a card that can thwart their strategy.

On December 6, an individual named Daniel Dukes was involved in a vehicular incident at the intersection of North 4th Street in New Orleans. Following the collision, a police officer intervened, and an investigation was launched. The lawyer representing Dukes, Steven Satterfield, revealed a surprising aspect of the case: Dukes' attire consisted of a jacket.

Subsequent to the incident, the New Orleans Police Department released graphic details about the traffic stop. Dukes had allegedly pulled out a firearm, prompting the officer to retrieve the weapon from his pocket. However, Satterfield clarified that Dukes had merely opened his jacket and attempted to place the gun away. The police were not investigating Dukes for any specific crime other than acting in a manner deemed "unwise."

To the media, these developments seemed clear-cut. The New Orleans police department was being transparent in its investigation; all parties involved were being accurately represented. However, Dukes' attire could have played a significant role in the outcome of the incident.

To begin with, Dukes was already a suspect in an unrelated incident that took place at the intersection prior to the collision. Police claimed he had discharged a firearm in search of an individual that night. (As the Times noted, some local critics have attributed the shooting death of a man in New Orleans by police officers for emboldening residents to seek revenge against law enforcement.) Given this, the mere disclosure by the police of Dukes' involvement in the incident at the intersection in the early stages of the investigation might have placed him at a higher risk for being targeted by police for any subsequent criminal activity.

The police did not have to disclose the attire of the suspect at all. The initial description of the suspect, provided by police, matched Dukes to varying degrees. This might seem minor, but it is crucial: Dukes wore a jacket, and the media focus tended to focus on the attire of any suspect immediately following the collision. Dukes might have been stopped more frequently for similar reasons. This might seem like a small detail, but it is the kind of systemic detail that could have easily influenced a judge, attorney, or jury's decision to convict Dukes. The jury ultimately found him not guilty after 10 minutes of deliberation.

But in that second, more immediate crash investigation, the evidence was against him. Satterfield stated that if the police had kept the details of the traffic stop secret, Dukes would have been killed. At the same time, the media also made light of the fact that Dukes wore a jacket, instead focusing on other aspects of his life: a woman named Markeisha Gaines, a substance abuse issue that had been escalating over the past several years, and other social ills from which Dukes was allegedly suffering.

If the media had known what was actually happening in the early stages, they might have done the opposite. There are many examples across the country of individuals engaging in harmful behavior, much of it violent. But stories about the victims are nearly always framed in relation to harmful behavior. The latter narrative is often the focus of the press because, in the absence of a mass harmful behavior, it tends to be the "progressive" narrative. As Michelle Alexander explained in her book, The New Jim Crow: Mass Incarceration in the Age of Colorblindness, the press tends to frame harmful behavior as being more serious and violent, in comparison to non-harmful behavior, which seems more minor and non-threatening.

When harmful behavior is discussed in the press, it is usually treated as isolated incidents rather than part of an ongoing pattern that can lead to greater disparities in criminal justice. But when there is a disproportionate amount of non-harmful behavior, it's often seen as part of a greater systemic pattern, which could lead to wider social change, such as fewer instances of harmful behavior by individuals. The disparity in the media's coverage in the aftermath of the collision in New Orleans would tend to support this belief.

Satterfield stated that some of the reports he received were vague and made no mention of attire, which he says indicates that "some people in the media were probably unaware." The term "bar staff" includes, but is not limited to, all of the following: staff members at a brewery who sell or offer to sell beverages, or employees of a hotel or motel who sell or offer to sell beverages, or all employees of any person selling beverages. "Bar staff" means an employee who is employed primarily as a staff member, or prepares beverages on or for premises where such beverages are sold or served, whether directly or indirectly, or who prepares or delivers beverages to patrons of a non-residence establishment.

The term "bar staff" also includes employees of retail establishments who have purchased from or are associated with that retail establishment, employees of hotel, motel, or retail establishment having an average nightly occupancy of twenty or more persons, employees of retail establishment having an average nightly occupancy of five hundred or more persons, or employees of other salespersons or employees of a retailer, manufacturer, and distributor.

The phenomenon of electron alignment within a semiconductor is crucial for efficient electron transfer across a conductive surface. The direction of electron rotation, typically not crucial in electron physics, plays a vital role in controlling electron flow. When electrons are aligned with the surface of the semiconductor, they exhibit a unique property known as polarization. This polarization difference enables the transfer of electrons from one position to another within the semiconductor.

The electric field within a semiconductor is directly proportional to its polarizability. In the absence of polarizability, the electric field remains constant regardless of the electron's location. This does not preclude the deposition of electric charge on the semiconductor surface, but it does reduce resistance to electron transfer between distant points on the surface and those at the bottom of the semiconductor.

Polarizability is measured by examining the direction of the electric field across the semiconductor. The field consists of two components: the electric field at the core and the electric field perpendicular to the planes of the semiconductor. One common semiconductor polarizability is the direction of the current, which is perpendicular to the plane of the semiconductor.

The electric field across a semiconductor is known as AC voltage, and its positive portion represents the polarization of electrons, while the negative portion represents the polarization of holes. The current in the semiconductor is known as DC voltage. The direction of the electric field is directly proportional to the polarizability of the semiconductor.

Polarizability is the electric polarization component, which is a vector multiplied by the electric field. Additionally, there are two other important aspects of an ideal, pure semiconductor that relate to polarization.

When the electric field at the core and outside the semiconductor is combined, it results in a component perpendicular to each other with the same direction. Such electrically conductive surfaces are known as superconductors. The electrical resistance in a current flowing through a superconductor is more than one volt per amp.

The electrical current is a linear function of electric polarizability and electric field. The polarity of the current depends on the polarity of the electric field. Therefore, the polarization of the electric field can significantly impact the potential for current flow through the semiconductor.

Electrons in a semiconductor are not perfectly aligned with the magnetic plane but are polarized by a small amount. Electrons on the surface of a semiconductor may be aligned in one of two ways: either in the "normal" position, which is the direction of rotation for the electron on the surface, or in an aligned position where the electric field is parallel to its surface.

If no electric field is present at the surface of the semiconductor, only one direction of rotation of the electrons may exist, but there will be no electrically conductive material at the point where the electron is located. This type of semiconductor will have many surface electrons, resulting in very low conductivity, known as a "quartz surface."
